docs.title: Sensor connection check
docs.text:
Not sure whether your battery device is online? Run this quick check. You restart the device and press its boot button, and the RGB light flashes a color that shows whether it's connected to Wi-Fi, to Homey, or to nothing. Select your device below. Each button name links to a page that shows where that button is.

TEMP-1BPLT-1B

1. Press the reset button and let go to restart the device.

2. Then press the boot button and let go.

1. Press the reset button and let go to restart the device.

2. Then press the boot button and let go.

The RGB light on your device then flashes a color that shows its connection status:

  • Blue: connected to Wi-Fi and Homey
  • Green: connected to Wi-Fi only, not to Homey
  • Yellow: no Wi-Fi connection

Read the first flash, not the second

A few seconds later the light flashes a second time, green or red. That second flash is the device's built-in sensor self-test, not its connection status, so read the connection status from the first color.

Keep your sensor awake with Prevent Sleep

To keep your sensor awake for extended periods of time, open the device in Homey, go to its settings, and turn on Prevent sleep under Battery settings (if battery is present). Homey can only change this setting while the sensor is awake, so press the reset button first. To learn more, see the Prevent Sleep guide for the TEMP-1, TEMP-1B, or PLT-1B.

docs.title: How To Wake Up Your Sensor
How to wake up your sensor
docs.text:
Once Prevent sleep is off, your Apollo TEMP-1B, PLT-1B, or BTN-1 sleeps between reports to make its battery last, and Homey can't reach it while it sleeps. In the Homey app, a sleeping sensor shows as Device disconnected, and if you try to change a setting, Homey shows The device is asleep. Settings can be changed when it next wakes up. The sensor wakes on its own after each Sleep duration and reconnects to Homey. Wake it yourself when you want fresh readings right away, or need it awake to change a setting, update the firmware, or troubleshoot.

Using a USB-powered TEMP-1?

Your TEMP-1 normally stays awake in Homey, so there's nothing to wake. If it keeps losing its connection to Homey, it may have been set to sleep earlier, for example in Home Assistant. Turn Prevent sleep back on with its boot button.

docs.title: Wake your sensor
docs.text:
Pressing the reset button restarts your sensor, so it wakes up right away, connects to your Wi-Fi, and reports to Homey. On a BTN-1, any of its four buttons wakes it too. The boot button can't wake a sleeping sensor. Once the sensor is awake, the boot button is what keeps it awake. Select your device below to find both buttons.

TEMP-1BPLT-1BBTN-1

The buttons are on the board inside the case. To reach the reset button, gently pry the lid off at the small slit near the top of the case. You can press the boot button with the lid off too, or with a paperclip through the small opening on the right side of the case when the USB-C port faces you. Putting the TEMP-1B in boot mode has more photos.

To wake the TEMP-1B, press and release the reset button. You can also take the battery out and put it back in.

This is the boot button, which you'll use to keep the sensor awake.

You can press both buttons with a pin through small openings in the case. Putting the PLT-1B in boot mode shows where the openings are.

To wake the PLT-1B, press and release the reset button. You can also take the battery out and put it back in.

The boot button, which you'll use to keep the sensor awake, sits next to the USB-C port.

To wake the BTN-1, press and release the reset button, on the left in the photo below. The boot button, which you'll use to keep the BTN-1 awake, is on the right.

Pressing Button 1, 2, 3, or 4 also wakes the BTN-1. Homey receives that press as a Click of that button once the BTN-1 reconnects, so any flow you've tied to a click of that button runs. Use the reset button when you only want to wake it.

Your sensor is now awake. Homey reconnects to it on its own, and the Homey app no longer shows it as Device disconnected. It doesn't stay awake for long, though. Unless Prevent sleep is on, it sends fresh readings and goes back to sleep about 20 seconds after Homey connects (about 10 seconds for the BTN-1), or after about 90 seconds if Homey doesn't connect at all. Not sure your TEMP-1B or PLT-1B woke up? The sensor connection check tells you in a few seconds.

docs.title: Keep your sensor awake
docs.text: A wake-up doesn't last long enough to change settings or troubleshoot comfortably. Turn on Prevent sleep and your sensor stays awake until you turn it off again. You can turn it on from the sensor itself or from the Homey app, where it sits in your sensor's Settings under Battery settings (if battery is present).

docs.title: With the buttons on the sensor
docs.text:
The buttons work even when Homey can't reach the sensor, which makes this the most reliable way. It's also the better choice for the BTN-1, which stays awake for only about 10 seconds after Homey connects. Press the two buttons one after the other, never together: holding the boot button while you press reset puts the sensor in boot mode for flashing firmware instead.

Watch how long you hold the boot button

Hold the boot button for 4 to 5 seconds, no longer. Holding it for 10 seconds or more resets your sensor to factory settings and erases its Wi-Fi, and you'd have to connect it to Wi-Fi again.

  1. Press and release the reset button to wake the sensor.
  2. Wait a few seconds, then press and hold the boot button for 4 to 5 seconds and let go.

Your sensor turns Prevent sleep on and stays awake. In Homey, Prevent sleep shows as checked once the sensor is connected. If Homey loses the connection again a few seconds later, the sensor was already on its way back to sleep. It still remembers Prevent sleep, so press the reset button once more and it stays awake this time.

docs.title: From the Homey app
docs.text:
The sensor stays awake for only about 20 seconds after Homey connects, or about 10 seconds for the BTN-1, so have the Homey app open and ready before you start.

  1. Wake the sensor with the reset button.
  2. In the Homey app, open your sensor and wait until it no longer shows Device disconnected.
  3. Right away, open its Settings, check Prevent sleep under Battery settings (if battery is present), and save.
  4. If Homey loses the connection again a few seconds later, press the reset button once more.

Your sensor now stays awake until you uncheck Prevent sleep again. If the sensor was already on its way back to sleep at step 3, it still keeps the change and starts up with Prevent sleep on after the reset in step 4. If Homey shows The device is asleep. Settings can be changed when it next wakes up. instead, the change didn't reach the sensor: start again from step 1, or use the buttons.

The Prevent sleep guide for the TEMP-1B, PLT-1B, or BTN-1 covers both settings in detail, including Sleep duration. On a BTN-1, Prevent sleep also decides which presses reach Homey.

Next step: let your sensor sleep again

Staying awake drains the battery far faster. Once you're done, turn Prevent sleep off and choose how long the sensor sleeps between reports.

TEMP-1B: Prevent sleep PLT-1B: Prevent sleep BTN-1: Prevent sleep

docs.title: TEMP-1 alert outside a temperature range
TEMP-1 alert outside a temperature range
docs.text:
Difficulty: Level 1

Your Apollo TEMP-1 sends its temperature probe reading to Homey about once a minute, and every new reading can start a flow. In this guide you build two flows in the Homey mobile app that keep watch on a freezer: the first sends a push notification when the probe gets too warm, the second when it gets too cold.

Before you start

  • Add your TEMP-1 to Homey with the Apollo Automation app. See Getting started.
  • Plug the temperature probe into the TEMP-1. Open your TEMP-1's Settings and, under Probes and offsets for TEMP-1 and TEMP-1B, set Select probe to Temperature. With Food selected, the temperature probe sends no readings.
  • Install the Homey mobile app on every phone that should get the alert.

docs.title: Pick your range
docs.text:
Find out what your freezer normally swings between before you set any limits. That way the alert only fires when something is actually wrong.

  1. Place the probe in the freezer and run its flat cable out through the door seal. Keep the TEMP-1 itself outside the freezer, somewhere cool and dry: only the probe and its cable can handle the cold.
  2. Leave it for a few hours so the reading settles. Most freezers should sit at or below -18 °C (0 °F).
  3. In Homey Insights, look at your TEMP-1's Temperature Probe history. Note the highest and lowest readings.
  4. Pick a maximum a little above the highest reading and a minimum a little below the lowest. This guide uses -10 °C and -30 °C; yours will likely differ.

You now have a range that covers normal use and flags a real problem.

Enter your limits in degrees Celsius

The Temperature Probe reading, and the Temperature token the flows below compare, are always in °C. If you think in Fahrenheit, convert first: -10 °C is 14 °F, and -30 °C is -22 °F.

docs.title: Flow 1: Too warm
docs.text:
This flow runs each time the probe reading changes, checks it against your maximum, and sends the alert when the freezer is too warm.

  1. In the Homey mobile app, tap Flow in the bottom bar, then tap + at the top right (or Create a Flow if you have none yet).
  2. Under When..., tap Add Card. Open Apollo Automation under Apps, and choose your TEMP-1.
  3. Choose the card Temperature probe changed. It hands the new reading to the rest of the flow as the Temperature token.
  4. Under And..., tap Add Card and add Homey's built-in condition for comparing numbers. Set it to check that the Temperature token is greater than -10.
  5. Under Then..., tap Add Card and choose Send Message to User from Push Notifications.
  6. Type a message, for example Check the freezer! The TEMP-1 probe reads, and add the Temperature token after it.
  7. Tap User and pick who gets the alert, such as Everyone, then tap the check mark at the top right.
  8. Tap Next. Name the flow, for example Freezer too warm, and tap Save Flow.

The flow now shows in My Flows. Any probe reading above -10 °C sends the alert to your phone.

docs.title: Flow 2: Too cold
docs.text:
The second flow mirrors the first. Build it the same way, with these changes:

  1. In the And... condition, check that the Temperature token is less than -30.
  2. Change the message, for example to The freezer is colder than usual. The TEMP-1 probe reads, followed by the Temperature token.
  3. Name the flow Freezer too cold and tap Save Flow.

Both ends of your range are now covered: you hear about it whether the freezer warms up or runs too cold.

Expect a reminder with each new reading

Temperature probe changed runs every time the reading changes, not only when it crosses your limit. While the probe stays out of range, every change sends another notification, up to once a minute, until the temperature is back inside your range. To pause the reminders while you deal with the freezer, switch the flow off in My Flows, and switch it back on afterwards.

docs.title: Test your flows
docs.text:
To check the alert without warming up your freezer, tap the play button next to a flow in My Flows. It runs its Then cards once, and a green check mark confirms it ran. Your phone gets the notification.

If a flow doesn't run when the freezer is out of range:

  • Check that Select probe is set to Temperature and that the Temperature Probe reading keeps updating.
  • Check that your limits are in °C.
  • Check that both flows are switched on in My Flows.

docs.title: Optional: sound the TEMP-1's buzzer too
docs.text:
The TEMP-1 can also raise the alarm on its own. When you turn this on, the sensor checks every probe reading against a minimum and maximum you store on the device and sounds a short siren from its buzzer when the reading is outside them. It works alongside your flows, so anyone near the freezer hears it even if their phone is on silent.

  1. Open your TEMP-1's Settings.
  2. Under Probes and offsets for TEMP-1 and TEMP-1B, set Minimum probe temperature and Maximum probe temperature in °C, for example -30 and -10.
  3. Under Temperature range and alarm settings for TEMP PRO-1, turn on Alarm when temperature outside configured range. The group is named for the TEMP PRO-1, but this setting also switches the TEMP-1's alarm on and off.

The TEMP-1 now sounds the siren with each probe reading outside your range, until the reading is back inside it.

Use the probe settings, not the TEMP PRO-1 ones

Minimum temperature and Maximum temperature in the TEMP PRO-1 group belong to the TEMP PRO-1 and don't change anything on a TEMP-1. Set the range with Minimum probe temperature and Maximum probe temperature instead.

Next step: know when dinner is ready

Your freezer is covered. The automation examples put the food probe to work: a flow that lights your TEMP-1 green and sends you one notification when your food reaches its target temperature.

Build the food probe flow

docs.title: Automation examples using a TEMP-1
docs.text:
Difficulty: Level 2

🌱 New here? Try these first:

TEMP-1 alert outside a temperature range Difficulty: Level 1

Your Apollo TEMP-1 sends every probe reading to Homey, and each new reading can start a flow. This page has two flows to build in the Homey mobile app: a freezer alert, and a food probe flow that lights the TEMP-1 green and messages you when dinner is almost ready.

Before you start

  • Add your TEMP-1 to Homey with the Apollo Automation app. See Getting started.
  • Install the Homey mobile app on every phone that should get a notification.
  • For the freezer flow, plug in the temperature probe. For the food flow, plug in the food probe.

docs.title: How probe readings reach Homey
docs.text:
The Apollo Automation app gives each probe its own reading on the TEMP-1 and its own trigger card. Which one reports depends on the Select probe setting: open your TEMP-1's Settings and find it under Probes and offsets for TEMP-1 and TEMP-1B.

Probe Reading in Homey Trigger card How often it reports Set Select probe to Temperature probe Temperature Probe Temperature probe changed About once a minute Temperature Food probe Food Probe Food probe changed Every few seconds Food

Both cards hand the new reading to the flow as a Temperature token, always in °C. The probe that isn't selected sends no readings, so its card never runs.

The cards run each time the reading changes, not only when it crosses your limit. That's why each flow below checks the Temperature token in an And... condition, and why the food flow adds a second condition so it alerts you once instead of every few seconds.

docs.title: Freezer over its maximum temperature
docs.text:
This flow sends a push notification whenever the freezer probe reads warmer than your maximum. It is Flow 1 from TEMP-1 alert outside a temperature range, which walks through every tap and shows you how to pick a limit that suits your freezer.

Column Card Set it to When... Temperature probe changed, from Apollo Automation for your TEMP-1 Nothing to set And... Homey's built-in condition for comparing numbers Temperature token greater than -10 Then... Send Message to User, from Push Notifications A message such as Check the freezer! with the Temperature token, sent to Everyone

Once it's saved, any probe reading above -10 °C sends the alert, with a reminder each time the reading changes until the freezer cools down again.

docs.title: Food probe reaches a target temperature
docs.text:
Chicken is safe to eat at 74 °C (165 °F), and it keeps rising a few degrees while it rests. This flow fires at 71 °C (160 °F) so you can take it off the heat in time. When the food probe gets there, the TEMP-1's light turns green and your phone gets one notification.

The light also stops the alert from repeating. The food probe reports every few seconds, so the flow only runs while the light is off; once the flow has turned it green, later readings leave it alone.

Keep the TEMP-1 away from the heat

Only the food probe and its cable can go on the grill or in the oven. Set the TEMP-1 itself somewhere cool and dry, such as a side shelf.

Before you build the flow, set Select probe to Food and check that the Food Probe reading on your TEMP-1 changes when you hold the probe tip in your hand.

  1. In the Homey mobile app, tap Flow in the bottom bar, then tap + at the top right (or Create a Flow if you have none yet).
  2. Under When..., tap Add Card. Open Apollo Automation under Apps, choose your TEMP-1, and choose Food probe changed.
  3. Under And..., tap Add Card and add Homey's built-in condition for comparing numbers. Set it to check that the Temperature token is greater than 71.
  4. Under And..., tap Add Card again. Find your TEMP-1 under Zones & Devices and choose its condition for whether it is turned on. Turn on Invert, so the card checks that the TEMP-1 is turned off. On a TEMP-1, turned on and off means its RGB light.
  5. Under Then..., tap Add Card. Find your TEMP-1 under Zones & Devices and choose Turn on.
  6. Under Then..., tap Add Card again. Choose Set a color for your TEMP-1, pick green, and tap the check mark.
  7. Under Then..., add Send Message to User from Push Notifications. Type a message such as Check the food! The food probe reads, add the Temperature token after it, and pick a User.
  8. Tap Next. Name the flow, for example Food is ready, and tap Save Flow.

The flow now shows in My Flows. When the food probe passes 71 °C, your TEMP-1 glows green and your phone gets one notification.

docs.title: Reset it for the next cook
docs.text: When the food is off the heat, open your TEMP-1 in the Homey app and turn it off, which turns its light off. With the light off, the flow is ready to alert you again. Between cooks, you can also switch the flow off in My Flows.

docs.title: Test your flows
docs.text:
To check the alert without cooking anything, tap the play button next to the flow in My Flows. It runs its Then cards once, and a green check mark confirms it ran: the TEMP-1 lights green and the notification arrives. Turn the TEMP-1's light off afterwards so the flow is ready for the real thing.

If a flow doesn't run:

  • Check that Select probe matches the probe the flow uses: Temperature for the freezer flow, Food for the food flow.
  • Check that your limits are in °C.
  • For the food flow, check that the TEMP-1's light is off before the food reaches its target.
  • Check that the flow is switched on in My Flows.

docs.title: Take it further
docs.text:
• More probes: with the Multi-Probe Splitter, the extra probes each get their own trigger card: Temperature probe 2 changed, Temperature probe 3 changed, and Temperature probe 4 changed. Build the freezer flow once per probe to watch a fridge and a freezer from one TEMP-1.
  • Other targets: change the number in the food flow's condition for other dishes, and give each one its own message.

docs.title: Coming from the Home Assistant cook chicken example
docs.text:
The Home Assistant version of the cook chicken example, shared by Discord user RalphP, does a few things the Homey flow above handles differently or leaves out:

  • A dashboard button to start and stop monitoring. In Homey, switch the flow on in My Flows when you start cooking and off when you're done.
  • A blinking light when the food is ready. The TEMP-1 has pulse effects for its light, but the Apollo Automation app has no card for them, so in Homey the light stays solid green.
  • A spoken announcement on smart speakers. The Home Assistant version uses text-to-speech. This guide doesn't cover speakers.

docs.title: Use cases for the TEMP-1
docs.text:
1. Monitoring fridge / freezer: There are settings to set the maximum temperature the sensor should reach. It can alert through the onboard buzzer if it rises above that temperature. The cable on the probe is flat to not interfere with fridge seals.

2. Monitoring fish tank, hot tub ( if covered ), pool ( if covered or in sealed box ) with the waterproof probe.

3. Monitoring grilling, baking, or other food activities with the food safe probe

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This will walk you through the process of connecting your new Apollo Automation sensor to Homey. If at any point you get stuck, join our Discord for some help.

docs.title: Connecting through hotspot:
docs.text:
To get your new Apollo sensor connected to your Wi-Fi, follow the steps below!

1. Plug the sensor into a quality power brick. They require 5v and under an amp so most phone chargers will be fine. ESP devices are sensitive to power fluctuations and users have had some issues with really cheap power bricks. If your device is restarting or unavailable please try a different power brick.

2. On your phone or PC, open the Wi-Fi settings and connect to "Apollo MSR2 Hotspot", it might take a minute for the Wi-Fi network to show up.

3. Once connected it should automatically open a dashboard for your sensor.

If this does not automatically open the dashboard, please open your web browser and go to http://192.168.4.1

4. Select the Wi-Fi network that you would like your sensor to connect to or scroll to the bottom and type in your Wi-Fi network then click "Save".

Tip for Mesh Wi-Fi systems or multiple Access Points

If you have multiple access points or a mesh system please manually type in your Wi-Fi network so it will join with the strongest signal!

5. Once connected, the sensor's dashboard will automatically close. You've successfully connected your sensor to your Wi-Fi.

docs.title: Adding Apollo Automation app in Homey:
docs.text:
You'll install the Apollo Automation app on your Homey from a desktop PC or a browser.

1. Navigate to this website and click "Install App". For now this needs to be done from a desktop PC or a browser.

2. Select the Homey device you want to install it on and then click "Install App" again!

3. Your device will install the Apollo Automation Homey App then move to the next section.

docs.title: Connecting to Homey:
docs.text:
Next, you'll add your Apollo sensor to Homey from the Homey app on your phone.

1. Open the Homey App on your phone and navigate to the Devices tab at the bottom then select the (+) icon in the top right and choose "New Device". Choose "Allow" if it pops up asking to find Bluetooth devices, or you can change this later in settings.

2. Select Apollo Automation under Brands in the bottom left then choose "Every Apollo Sensor". When prompted, click "Connect".

3. Your Apollo devices will automatically show up and if not, please first connect it to your Wi-Fi following the steps outlined here.

4. Select the device you want to add, in this case an Apollo MTR-1 and click Continue at the bottom.

5. Click Continue Setup and choose a Zone to place your device in. If you are new to Homey you can choose Home and move it to another Zone later after you create more zones!

6. Change any other default settings like the Name, icon, etc or click Finish in the bottom right.

7. You are done! Your sensor is now ready to create flows and add as a favorite to your dashboard!

Click here to join our Discord for fast support!

docs.title: Prevent sleep
docs.text: Your Apollo TEMP-1 runs on USB power, but its firmware can still sleep between readings: it wakes up, reports, and goes back to sleep. Sleeping keeps the board from warming itself up, so the board temperature reads closer to the room. The TEMP-1 ships with Prevent sleep on, so it stays awake and reports all the time.

docs.title: Sleep isn't available for the TEMP-1 in Homey
docs.text:
In Homey, your TEMP-1 stays awake. You'll see Prevent sleep and Sleep duration in your TEMP-1's Settings in the Homey app, under Battery settings (if battery is present), but the Apollo Automation app only lets you change Prevent sleep on a sensor with a battery. If you uncheck it on the TEMP-1, Homey refuses the change and shows Battery settings are not supported on this device.

Staying awake is how Homey expects a USB-powered sensor to work, so there's nothing you need to change here.

Leave Sleep duration as it is

Homey shows Sleep duration in hours, but the TEMP-1 reads the number as minutes: the default of 8 means 8 minutes. It only applies while Prevent sleep is off, so you don't need to change it in Homey.

Using Home Assistant too?

Home Assistant can turn sleep on for the TEMP-1. See the Home Assistant Prevent Sleep guide. While the TEMP-1 sleeps, Homey loses its connection between reports.

docs.title: Correct the board temperature instead
docs.text:
If you wanted sleep to stop the board's own warmth from nudging the temperature up, an offset fixes the reading without it. You need a reference thermometer you trust.

  1. Put the reference thermometer next to your TEMP-1 and give both time to settle.
  2. Compare the TEMP-1's temperature reading in Homey with the reference. Use the board reading, not a probe.
  3. In your TEMP-1's Settings, under Probes and offsets for TEMP-1 and TEMP-1B, set Board temperature offset to how many degrees Celsius the TEMP-1 reads too high, and save. For example, if the TEMP-1 shows 23.5 °C and the reference shows 22 °C, enter 1.5.

The TEMP-1's temperature in Homey now matches your reference thermometer. The offset only changes the board reading, not a probe plugged into the TEMP-1.

Homey set to Fahrenheit?

The offset is always in degrees Celsius. Divide the difference you see in °F by 1.8: a reading 2.7 °F too high is an offset of 1.5.

docs.title: If your TEMP-1 was set to sleep before
docs.text:
If Prevent sleep was turned off earlier, for example in Home Assistant, the TEMP-1 remembers it and keeps sleeping after you add it to Homey, so Homey keeps losing the connection. Homey can't change Prevent sleep on the TEMP-1, so turn it back on with the boot button. Putting the TEMP-1 in boot mode shows where the button is.

Don't hold the boot button while you plug in

Plugging in with the boot button held puts the TEMP-1 in boot mode for flashing firmware instead. Also let go before 10 seconds: holding the boot button that long resets the TEMP-1 to factory settings and erases its Wi-Fi.

  1. Unplug the TEMP-1 and plug it back in to wake it.
  2. Wait a few seconds, then press and hold the boot button for 4 to 5 seconds and let go.

The TEMP-1 turns Prevent sleep back on and stays connected to Homey, and Prevent sleep shows as checked in its settings. If Homey loses the connection again a few seconds later, the TEMP-1 was already on its way back to sleep. It still remembers Prevent sleep, so unplug it and plug it back in once more, and it stays awake this time.

Keep your TEMP-1 dry

Don't leave the TEMP-1 outside for long periods or let it get wet. If it will sit in damp air or could see rain, put it inside another, protective case.

docs.title: Sensor definitions
docs.text:
Once added to Home Assistant you can configure different settings for your TEMP-1. Use the tabs below to see what each entity does, grouped the same way Home Assistant displays them.

How often readings update

The Default Update column is how often each sensor refreshes while the TEMP-1 is awake. By default Prevent Sleep is on, so the device stays awake and reports continuously at these intervals. Turn Prevent Sleep off to let the TEMP-1 deep-sleep between readings for more accurate onboard AHT20 temperature and humidity (the ESP chip's heat skews them while it is awake); it then wakes for about 90 seconds, reports, and sleeps for the Sleep Duration.

To update firmware on a sleeping device, click Update on the Firmware Update entity and it installs the next time the device wakes (the firmware keeps itself awake until the update finishes, so you don't need to do anything else). The optional OTA helper is a separate toggle that overrides Prevent Sleep to keep a device awake on demand.

ControlsSensorsConfigurationDiagnostic Control What it does RGB Light One RGB Neopixel LED. Click the light bulb or color wheel to change the color. Use the toggle to turn it on or off. Alarm Outside Temp Range Sounds the onboard buzzer when the selected probe reads outside the Min Probe Temp to Max Probe Temp range. Use the toggle to turn it on or off. Defaults to off. Select Probe Chooses which probe the TEMP-1 reads: Temperature (the Dallas DS18B20 probe, available in long or short versions) or Food (the stainless steel, food-safe probe for grilling and cooking). Sensor Default Update Details Board Temperature 60s Onboard air temperature from the AHT20. Adjusted by the Board Temperature Offset. Board Humidity 60s Onboard relative humidity from the AHT20. Adjusted by the Board Humidity Offset. Temperature Probe 60s Reading from the Dallas DS18B20 probe. Active when Select Probe is set to Temperature. Adjusted by the Temp Probe Offset. Ideal for fridge/freezer and aquatic monitoring. Food Probe 3s Reading from the stainless steel, food-safe NTC probe. Active when Select Probe is set to Food. Adjusted by the Food Probe Offset. Designed for grilling, baking, and other cooking. Temperature Probe 2 60s Second Dallas DS18B20 probe on the one-wire bus. Disabled by default. Temperature Probe 3 60s Third Dallas DS18B20 probe on the one-wire bus. Disabled by default. Temperature Probe 4 60s Fourth Dallas DS18B20 probe on the one-wire bus. Disabled by default. Setting Default What it does ESP Reboot — Restarts the device. Helpful for troubleshooting or refreshing the connection. Board Temperature Offset 0.0 °C Calibrates the Board Temperature reading to a known value. Range is -70 to +70 °C. Board Humidity Offset 0 % Calibrates the Board Humidity reading to a known value. Range is -70 to +70 %. Temp Probe Offset 0.0 °C Calibrates the Temperature Probe reading to a known value. Range is -70 to +70 °C. Disabled by default. Food Probe Offset 0.0 °C Calibrates the Food Probe reading to a known value. Range is -70 to +70 °C. Disabled by default. Max Probe Temp 125.0 °C Upper threshold for the Alarm Outside Temp Range toggle. Min Probe Temp -55.0 °C Lower threshold for the Alarm Outside Temp Range toggle. Probe Temp Difference Threshold 0.0 °C Temperature change that triggers a report when Notify Only Outside Temp Difference is on. Disabled by default. Notify Only Outside Temp Difference Off Wakes the device to report only when the probe temperature changes by more than the Probe Temp Difference Threshold, instead of every wake cycle. Disabled by default. Sleep Duration 8 min How long the TEMP-1 stays in deep sleep between wake cycles (only used when Prevent Sleep is off). Prevent Sleep On Keeps the device awake instead of deep-sleeping, so it reports continuously. Turn it off to let the TEMP-1 deep-sleep between readings for more accurate onboard AHT20 temperature and humidity. Factory Reset ESP — Erases settings and returns the device to factory firmware defaults. Disabled by default. Entity Default Update What it shows Apollo Firmware Version on boot The Apollo firmware build installed on the device (for example, 26.3.2.1). ESPHome Version on boot The ESPHome version the firmware was compiled with. Firmware Update — Shows whether a firmware update is available and lets you update from inside Home Assistant. IP Address on connect The device's IP address on your network. Online on change Connection status of the device to Home Assistant. RSSI 60s Wi-Fi signal strength in dBm. Values closer to 0 are stronger; a weak signal can affect reliability. ESP Temperature 60s Internal temperature of the ESP32 chip. Runs warmer than the room because of the processor and Wi-Fi radio. Uptime 60s How long the device has been running since its last reboot.

Join our Discord if you need more help!

docs.title: Putting the TEMP-1 in boot mode
Putting the TEMP-1 in boot mode
docs.text:
This will cover how to put the TEMP-1 into boot mode.

This is needed to force the device into boot mode to reflash the firmware.

docs.title: Method 1: Boot button only
docs.text:
You can put your device into boot mode with only the boot button and a paperclip.

1. Position the TEMP-1 so that the USB-C port is facing you. On the right side of the device, locate a small opening where you can use a paperclip to press the boot button.

If you prefer, please remove the lid by gently prying up on the small slit by the top of the case.

2. Push and hold the boot button. While still holding the button down, plug in a USB-C cable into the USB-C port of your TEMP-1 then let go of the button.

3. Continue with uploading the firmware document.

docs.title: Method 2: Boot and reset buttons
docs.text:
You can also open the case and put your device into boot mode by holding the boot button down while you press and release the reset button.

1. Unplug the device and remove the case as shown in the images above

2. Plug it into your computer.

3. Put your TEMP-1 in boot mode. Use both buttons, in this order:

  • Press and hold the boot button (labeled BOOT, shown above). Keep holding it.
  • While you're still holding boot, press and release the reset button (labeled RST, at the opposite end of the board from boot).
  • Let go of boot.

Keep holding boot the whole time

Pressing reset by itself only restarts the TEMP-1. It goes into boot mode only when boot is held down while you press and release reset.

4. Continue with uploading the firmware document.

docs.title: Factory re-flash TEMP-1
docs.text:
If your device becomes unresponsive and you've exhausted the other troubleshooting methods you can reflash the factory firmware by following the below guide.

This needs to be done in Chrome, Edge, or another Chromium based browser.

If your device has already been added to Homey, please remove it from Homey before continuing.

Follow these steps to put your device in boot mode and install the factory firmware.

1. Put your device in boot mode by holding down the boot button and then plugging in the USB cable.

2. Navigate to the Apollo TEMP-1 installer.

3. Choose USB Power since you are using a TEMP-1, then click Connect & Install.

Use R2 version unless instructed to use R1 by support!

The Apollo installer installs the Revision 2 (R2) firmware. R2 is what all of our devices use except a very small batch of TEMP-1 and TEMP-1B boards. If support tells you your board needs Revision 1 (R1), click Connect under Non Battery Firmware Revision 1 on the classic TEMP-1 installer instead. In the next steps, the firmware option is named Install ApolloAutomation.TEMP-1.

4. Select the open com port then click Connect.

5. Click Install Apollo.TEMP-1_R2.

6. Click "INSTALL".

7. Once you see "Installation complete!" you are finished. Click Next then close out of the browser window.

Power cycle your device before doing anything else!

Your device is still in boot mode and needs to be power cycled aka power removed to make it boot in a normal mode!

8. Please proceed to the getting started guide and set up your sensor as a new device!

docs.title: Reset Wi-Fi credentials on your TEMP-1
Reset Wi-Fi credentials on your TEMP-1
docs.text:
You can clear the Wi-Fi details saved on your device and connect it to a new Wi-Fi network through its hotspot.

1. Plug the device into power.

2. Long press the Boot button for 10 seconds

3. The Wi-Fi credentials should be reset and it will broadcast its hotspot again.

4. Connect to the hotspot titled "Apollo TEMP1 Hotspot" and enter your new Wi-Fi details!

docs.title: TEMP-1B FAQ
docs.text:
1. How is the TEMP-1B powered?

  • The TEMP-1B operates with a rechargeable 16340 Flat Top battery (not included), giving it portability for temp monitoring without being tied to an outlet.

2. How long does the battery last in the TEMP-1B?

  • Battery life depends on sleep/wake intervals. Waking every 12 hours provides around 6+ months of battery life.

3. Can you charge the battery by plugging in the device?

  • No, you cannot charge the battery through the USB port. You need a separate 16340 charger such as a nitecore 2 or 4 bay.

4. What are the Optional Probe Addons?

  • 1.5m (~5ft) Waterproof Flat Cable (DS18B20) – -55°C to 85°C (-67°F to 185°F), ±0.5°C accuracy. Ideal for fridges, freezers, fish tanks etc.
  • 20cm (~8in) Waterproof Flat Cable (DS18B20) – -55°C to 85°C (-67°F to 185°F), ±0.5°C accuracy.
  • 1m (~3ft) Stainless Steel Food-Safe Probe (NTC) – Max 350°C (662°F). Perfect for grilling, baking, and food prep (not dishwasher safe).

5. Is the TEMP-1B weatherproof? Can I use it outdoors?

  • The TEMP-1B is primarily designed for indoor use, but the waterproof DS18B20 temperature probes are suited for harsh conditions. The main body is not rated for outdoor use without additional protection.

6. How does the TEMP-1B connect to Homey?

  • The TEMP-1B joins your Wi-Fi, and the Apollo Automation app for Homey talks to it directly over your local network through the ESPHome native API, with no cloud account. Once you add it, its readings show up on the device in Homey, ready for flows and Insights. The app runs on Homey Pro; Homey Cloud isn't supported.

Next step: add your TEMP-1B to Homey

Connect the sensor to your Wi-Fi through its hotspot, then add it with the Apollo Automation app. The getting started guide walks you through both.

Get started with Homey

7. How often does the TEMP-1B send sensor data?

  • A new TEMP-1B ships with Prevent sleep checked, so it stays awake and reports most readings every 60 seconds. That drains the battery fast. Once you uncheck Prevent sleep, the TEMP-1B wakes up, sends its readings to Homey, and goes back to sleep to save battery. How long it sleeps is the Sleep duration setting, in hours (12 by default). Both settings are under Battery settings (if battery is present) in the device's Settings in the Homey app. A shorter sleep gives fresher readings and a shorter battery life. See Prevent sleep for the details.

Change settings while the TEMP-1B is awake

Homey can only send a setting while the sensor is awake and connected. If it's asleep, Homey shows The device is asleep. Settings can be changed when it next wakes up. Keep the sensor awake and try again.

8. Can I customize the TEMP-1B’s functionality?

  • Absolutely! With ESPHome, users can modify firmware, settings, and even print custom cases for the TEMP-1B. Our YAML is on GitHub and our .STEP and .STL CAD files are available for community use.

9. What are the RGB LED and piezo buzzer used for?

  • The RGB LED is the TEMP-1B's light in Homey. Turn it on or off, dim it, or change its color from the device or in a flow. Commands reach the sensor only while it's awake.
  • The piezo buzzer sounds an alarm on its own when the probe temperature goes above or below a range you set. In the device's Settings in the Homey app, set Minimum probe temperature and Maximum probe temperature (in °C), then check Alarm when temperature outside configured range. The alarm watches the probe chosen in Select probe, and it checks each time the sensor is awake and takes a reading. Homey flows can't play the buzzer themselves.

The alarm checkbox is listed under TEMP PRO-1

Alarm when temperature outside configured range sits in the group Temperature range and alarm settings for TEMP PRO-1, but it works on the TEMP-1B too. The minimum and maximum are under Probes and offsets for TEMP-1 and TEMP-1B. For a full walkthrough, see TEMP-1B alert outside a temperature range.

10. Is the TEMP-1B compatible with other smart home platforms?

  • Yes. Besides Homey (through the Apollo Automation app), the TEMP-1B works with Home Assistant, and it may work with other platforms through the ESPHome API or MQTT. See Supported platforms.

11. Do I need coding knowledge to use the TEMP-1B?

  • No. Adding the TEMP-1B to Homey and building flows takes no code. YAML knowledge only matters if you want to customize the firmware with ESPHome.

12. Can I access data from the TEMP-1B remotely?

  • Yes. The TEMP-1B reports to your Homey over your local network, and the Homey app shows its latest readings wherever you are, as long as your Homey is reachable remotely.

13. What’s the difference between the battery and non-battery versions?

  • The TEMP-1B is battery-operated and slightly larger, while the non-battery (NB) version is compact and requires USB-C power at 5 volts using 1amp or less (5W). They both have the same components: a 3.5mm port for the waterproof temperature probe or the food probe, plus onboard air temperature and humidity.

14. Can I use multiple TEMP-1B sensors with one Homey?

  • Yes. Add each TEMP-1B with the Apollo Automation app. Each one shows up as its own device in Homey, so you can monitor several fridges, freezers, rooms, or other spaces.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The TEMP-1B (16340 battery) can be used with an optional temperature probe which comes in two lengths or a food safe grill probe. The TEMP-1B itself can be used with an optional magnetic mount to mount it to a fridge, grill, or other surface while taking measurements. It also features an AHT20-F air temperature and humidity sensor, which includes dust protection, an RGB LED, and a piezo buzzer.

Optional Probe Addons:

  • 1.5m (~5ft) Waterproof Flat Cable (DS18B20): -55°C to 85°C (-67°F to 185°F), ±0.5°C accuracy. Ideal for fridges, freezers, fish tanks etc.
  • 20cm (~8in) Waterproof Flat Cable (DS18B20): -55°C to 85°C (-67°F to 185°F), ±0.5°C accuracy.
  • 1m (~3ft) Stainless Steel Food-Safe Probe (NTC): Max 350°C (662°F). Perfect for grilling, baking, and food prep (not dishwasher safe).

Do not leave your sensor outside or let it get wet!

The TEMP-1B should not be left outside for long periods of time or allowed to get wet. You will need to use another case around your TEMP-1B if there will be high moisture content in the air or if it is expected to rain.

docs.title: TEMP-1B food probe
docs.text:
The TEMP-1B comes with an optional food probe which can be used to monitor food temperatures when baking, grilling, etc. It includes a heat-resistant cable but the TEMP-1B itself needs to stay in a cool environment.

1. To use your food probe, take it out of the package and insert it into the 3.5mm port on your TEMP-1B.

2. Once inserted, proceed to step 3 unless you have a battery in it

If you are using it with a battery you need to push the reset button.

The TEMP-1B looks for the food probe when it boots and if it is not there then the sensor is marked as failed and will not report a temperature. You need to click the reset button if you have a battery in it or power cycle your TEMP-1B to make it reliably use the new food temperature probe.

3. In the Homey app, open your TEMP-1B's Settings and, under Probes and offsets for TEMP-1 and TEMP-1B, set Select probe to Food.

Do not leave your sensor outside or let it get wet!

The TEMP-1B should not be left outside for long periods of time or allowed to get wet. You will need to use another case around your TEMP-1B if there will be high moisture content in the air or if it is expected to rain.

docs.title: TEMP-1B magnetic mount
docs.text:
The TEMP-1B comes with an optional magnetic mount which can be used to secure the TEMP-1B to your fridge or grill as shown below.

1. To use your magnetic mount place it with the magnet facing upwards as shown:

2. Align the lid with the hole in the top right and place your TEMP-1B inside the magnetic mount and gently press down.

3. It will sit flush as shown in the image below.

4. Affix your TEMP-1B to the outside of a fridge or a safe cool place on the grill.

Do not leave your sensor outside or let it get wet!

The TEMP-1B should not be left outside for long periods of time or allowed to get wet. You will need to use another case around your TEMP-1B if there will be high moisture content in the air or if it is expected to rain.

docs.title: TEMP-1 multi-probe splitter guide
docs.text:
The TEMP-1 comes with an optional 3.5mm Multi-Probe Splitter which can be used to monitor a fridge, freezer, fish tank, pool, hot tub, etc with up to 4 probes.

Firmware version 25.11.20.1 or newer required for TEMP-1 and TEMP-1B

The multi probe support was added in November of 2025. If you are using an old TEMP-1 or TEMP-1B that hasn't been updated then please visit our reflashing guide for the TEMP-1 and TEMP-1B. Alternatively you can update your devices following this guide!

1. To use your TEMP-1 Multi-Probe Splitter gently plug it into the 3.5mm port on your device.

2. Plug in your long or short temp probes into the Multi-Probe Splitter.

Power on your TEMP-1 after plugging in all of your probes!

The TEMP-1 will look for the probes at boot and mark them failed if you power on and plug in the probes after. Power cycle your device and they should show up!

3. Go to the device page of your TEMP-1 in Home Assistant and confirm the Temperature Probe is selected from the dropdown.

4. Enable the disabled 3rd and 4th temp probe entities if you have more than 2 probes!

5. Once completed you will see all four probes updating the temperature!

6. To rename the probes you can edit each probe and choose a unique name such as "Fridge Probe" and "Freezer Probe" as shown below!

Do not leave your sensor outside or let it get wet!

The TEMP-1 should not be left outside for long periods of time or allowed to get wet. You will need to use another case around your TEMP-1 if there will be high moisture content in the air or if it is expected to rain.

docs.title: TEMP-1B temp probe
docs.text:
The TEMP-1B comes with an optional temp probe which can be used to monitor a fridge, freezer, fish tank, pool, hot tub, etc. It includes a protected cable but the TEMP-1B itself needs to stay in a cool environment.

1. To use your temp probe, take it out of the package and insert it into the 3.5mm port on your TEMP-1B.

2. Once inserted, proceed to step 3 unless you have a battery in it

If you are using it with a battery you need to push the reset button.

The TEMP-1B looks for the temp probe when it boots and if it is not there then the sensor is marked as failed and will not work properly in Home Assistant. You need to click the reset button if you have a battery in it or power cycle your TEMP-1B to make it reliably use the new temperature probe.

3. Go to the device page of your TEMP-1B in Home Assistant and choose the Temperature Probe.

Do not leave your sensor outside or let it get wet!

The TEMP-1B should not be left outside for long periods of time or allowed to get wet. You will need to use another case around your TEMP-1B if there will be high moisture content in the air or if it is expected to rain.

Example images of the long temperature probe in a mini freezer:

docs.title: Probe pinout
docs.text:
The 1.5m and 20cm DS18B20 temp probes use a standard 3.5mm TRS plug. Wire yours the same way if you're building your own probe or repairing a cut cable.
