  • 24 (unchanged): the new value matched the old one, so nothing was written.
  • 100 → 15 (was off): that gate was turned off (set to 100) and calibration turned it back on. A line under the table says so and how to turn it off again.
  • 100 (off) or 40 → 100 (off): the background at that gate was so strong the threshold went to the top of the scale, so that gate can no longer trigger. On an MSR-1 or MSR-2, the G0 and G1 still thresholds often end up here, because those gates sit right at the sensor and their still energy idles near the top. That's normal and needs no action, so the card does not warn about them. For any other gate in use, including G0 and G1 move, the card warns you (see Warnings the card can show).
  • no data: the gate sent too few readings, so it was left as it was.
  • (spike seen) after a peak: one reading jumped well above the rest, as if something moved. The threshold still comes from that peak, so that gate ends up less sensitive. If nothing should have moved there, run the calibration again with the room empty.
  • not confirmed (radar offline) or (not confirmed): the radar did not report the new value back. See Thresholds did not change on the radar.

Gates outside the range the radar is set to use are dimmed, with a note under the table such as G7, G8: not used (beyond Max Move Gate 6). They are still calibrated, so they are ready if you extend the range later.

docs.title: Check the result or undo it
docs.text:
Under the table, the card suggests a walk test:

Now walk around, then sit still for a minute: the Radar Target row in Target / Occupancy should stay on the whole time you are in the room and turn off a few seconds after you leave (Radar Timeout).

  1. Press Turn on Radar Engineering Mode on the Gate Energy chart if you'd like to watch the gates as well.
  2. Walk through the room, then sit where you usually sit and stay still for a minute or two. Radar Target covers still presence as well as movement, so it should stay on the whole time. With Radar Engineering Mode on, the bars of the gates you're in should be outlined.
  3. Leave the room. Radar Target should turn off a few seconds later, once Radar Timeout runs out, and no gate inside the radar's range should stay outlined.
  4. If you turned on Radar Engineering Mode, press Turn off Radar Engineering Mode on the Radar setup card, or use the switch on the Controls card.

Below the walk-test line are three buttons: Undo (restore your previous values), Calibrate again (a fresh calibration with a new countdown and listen), and Close. If the radar now misses you, or behaves worse than before, press Undo (restore your previous values). The card shows Restoring saved thresholds... 3 of 16 and then Restored your previous values. Undo saves the values it replaces first, so the button then reads Redo (put the calibrated values back), and pressing it puts the calibrated values back. The saved copy survives a Home Assistant restart.

If someone walked in during the listen, press Stop: nothing is written before the writing stage. If you only notice afterward, press Undo, clear the room, and press Calibrate with empty room.

The next time you open the dashboard, the card starts on its checklist again with a line such as Last calibrated Oct 11, 02:32 PM, 16 of 18 thresholds changed. (in your browser's date and time format), the Undo (restore your previous values) button with the time those values were saved under it (Saved Oct 11, 02:31 PM.), and Show last result to open the last result table.

docs.title: Warnings the card can show
docs.text:
Warnings appear under the result table. Each one is a sign the result may not match your empty room:

  • The radar reported someone present for 40% of the listen. If someone was in the room, even sitting still, press Undo and run it again. The radar detected presence for more than a quarter of the listen. That is normal for a radar that was too sensitive (which is what you are fixing), but if a person or pet was in the room, the thresholds are too high. Press Undo, clear the room, and run it again. If you're sure the room was empty, keep the result and do the walk test in Check the result or undo it.
  • The G3 move threshold is now off (its background peaked at 92). If a fan or curtain moves there all day this is fine; if not, press Undo and run again with the room really empty. That gate can no longer detect anything. If something at that distance moves all day, that is the expected result. If not, something moved there during the listen: press Undo and run it again with the room empty.
  • The radar was unavailable for part of the listen; gates with too few readings were left as they were. The radar dropped off the network for a moment. Gates marked no data kept their old thresholds. Check the radar's connection and run it again.
  • The G2 still threshold was off (set to 100) and calibration turned it back on (now 15). If you turned it off on purpose, set it back to 100 on the Still Thresholds card, or press Undo to put back all your previous values. You had that gate turned off, and calibration set it like every other gate. If you want it off, set it back to 100 on the card the line names. A preview words it as what calibration would do.
  • 2 values could not be confirmed: G3 move threshold reads back 35 (asked for 27), G5 still threshold could not be read (radar offline). Check the Move / Still Thresholds cards. The radar did not report some of the new values back. The heading reads Thresholds updated, 2 could not be confirmed. Check those gates on the threshold cards, and press Undo or run it again once the radar is stable.

docs.title: A tour of the radar tab
docs.text: Open Apollo mmWave from your sidebar and, if you have more than one radar, pick your radar's tab. On a wide screen the cards sit in columns; on a phone they stack in the order below. Card titles start with the name of the radar chip: LD2410 on an MSR-1 or MSR-2, LD2412 on an R PRO-1. A card only shows rows for entities Home Assistant has, so a setting the firmware hides has no row.

docs.title: First column
docs.text:
• Start here: your sensor's name and its first steps, pictured at the top of this guide. It ends with two links. Full tuning guide → opens this guide on the wiki: on an MSR-1 or MSR-2 the general version, the one that covers every Apollo radar, and on an R PRO-1 the R PRO-1 version at its LD2412 section. All settings for this device → opens the sensor's own page in Home Assistant, where every setting the dashboard leaves out lives. On an R PRO-1, the card also says what each radar is for and which presence sensor to use in automations.
  • Radar setup: checks the radar's settings and offers a fix (see Start with the Radar setup card).
  • Auto-calibrate: the calibration card. It shows the chip and the device name under its title, a short checklist, and the Calibrate with empty room button. Everything about it is in Calibrate with an empty room above.

  • LD2410 Controls: the Radar Engineering Mode switch, plus Radar Bluetooth (HLK app), Restart Radar, and Factory Reset Radar. On an R PRO-1 the card also has Start Dynamic Background Correction and Background Correction Running (see R PRO-1 and its LD2412 radar). Radar Bluetooth (HLK app) is the radar chip's own Bluetooth for the HLK phone app, not your sensor's Bluetooth proxy. Restart Radar restarts the radar chip without changing any settings. Leave Factory Reset Radar alone unless Apollo support asks you to press it: it puts the radar chip's settings, every threshold included, back to factory values, so run Calibrate with empty room again if it happens. Both ask before they act. The restart for the whole sensor is on the Device card at the bottom of the tab.

  • LD2410 Zone Config (MSR-1 and MSR-2): Start Zone 1, End Zone 1, End Zone 2, and End Zone 3 split the radar's range into three distance bands, each with its own occupancy sensor (Radar Zone 1 Occupancy to Radar Zone 3 Occupancy). These are distances from the sensor, not areas you draw like on the R PRO-1 and MTR-1 zone map. The boxes are in cm, even when Home Assistant uses feet, and the zones sit back to back: Zone 1 runs from Start Zone 1 to End Zone 1, Zone 2 from there to End Zone 2, and Zone 3 from there to End Zone 3. They're optional: leave them as they are unless you want separate sensors for, say, the couch and the far end of the room.

docs.title: Second column
docs.text:
• LD2410 Distances: a chart laid out along the radar's range. From top to bottom it can show a Zones row with your three distance bands (Z1 to Z3, with a filled circle when someone is in that band), bars for the current Detection, Moving, and Still distance, the Gates row, and bars that mark how far the radar is set to look (Max Move and Max Still, or Max Gate and Min Gate on an R PRO-1). On a computer, hover over a row for a short explanation. Distances show in meters, or in inches if Home Assistant uses US units.

  • LD2410 Detection Range: Radar Timeout (how long presence stays on after the last detection), the gate size (hidden until you enable its entity), and the sliders that set how far the radar looks: Max Move Gate and Max Still Gate on an MSR-1 or MSR-2, Max Gate and Min Gate on an R PRO-1. The sliders start locked under a Sliders locked row (see Set the range and timeout). A note under the card explains each one and gives each gate's depth in your units.

  • LD2410 Target / Occupancy: Radar Target (anyone detected), Radar Moving Target, Radar Still Target, and on an MSR-1 or MSR-2 Radar Zone 1 Occupancy to Radar Zone 3 Occupancy and Any zone, which is on while someone is in any of the three zones. A row lights up while it's on. On an R PRO-1 this card sits in the first column instead.

docs.title: Third column
docs.text:
• LD2410 Gate Energy: the chart you tune with. Each gate has two bars, a purple one for move energy and a green one for still energy, on a 0 to 100 scale. While Radar Engineering Mode is on, a right-pointing triangle marks each gate's move threshold and a left-pointing triangle its still threshold, and a bar that rises above its threshold gets an outline in the threshold's color: outlined bar = above threshold (detecting). While Radar Engineering Mode is off, the chart is dimmed with Turn on Radar Engineering Mode to see gate energy values and a Turn on Radar Engineering Mode button you can press right there.
  • LD2410 Move Thresholds: one slider per gate (G0 to G8 on an MSR-1 or MSR-2, G0 to G13 on an R PRO-1) to set each gate's move threshold. Each row is named for how far out its gate reaches, from G0 (at the sensor) to G8 (about 6 m), in feet when Home Assistant uses US customary units. The sliders start locked, like the Detection Range ones. A note underneath recaps how thresholds work.

docs.title: Fourth column
docs.text:
• LD2410 Occupancy History: the last 24 hours of Detected, Moving, and Still (and, on an MSR-1 or MSR-2, Any zone and Zone 1 to Zone 3), so a false trigger overnight is still there in the morning. On an R PRO-1 it's titled Occupancy History, its lines read LD2412 Presence, LD2412 Moving, and LD2412 Still, and it also shows LD2450 Presence and each zone you drew.
  • LD2410 Still Thresholds: one slider per gate for the still thresholds, named and locked the same way.
  • Device: at the bottom of every tab. It shows Apollo firmware, the radar chip's firmware (LD2410 firmware on an MSR-1 or MSR-2, LD2450 firmware on an MTR-1; on an R PRO-1, both chips' versions are hidden until you enable them on the device page), and Firmware update, which opens Home Assistant's own update window when you tap it. An MTR-1 has no Firmware update row. Restart device restarts the whole sensor after you confirm. On an R PRO-1 with the LD2412 it reads Restart device (both radars), and on an MTR-1 or an R PRO-1 without the LD2412 it reads Restart device (also restarts the radar). Under the rows are the All settings for this device → link and how to download a support file. While the Wi-Fi signal is below -75 dBm, a Weak Wi-Fi note appears too.

On an R PRO-1, the Zone Map heading comes right after the first column, with the LD2450's own Radar setup card, the zone map, Zone presence, LD2450 Live, and LD2450 Controls, so on a phone you reach them before the LD2412's threshold cards (see Draw zones on the R PRO-1 and MTR-1). An MTR-1 tab has those cards, its own Start here, and the Device card, without the tuning cards.

docs.title: R PRO-1 and its LD2412 radar
docs.text:
Every R PRO-1 has an LD2450 radar, and the optional LD2412 addon adds a second one. The LD2412 handles presence and gets the tuning cards and the calibration, and the LD2450 tracks positions for the zone map. An R PRO-1 without the LD2412 still shows the LD2412 cards on its tab, but there's no radar behind them, so the calibration and this section don't apply to it; its Start here card gives the zone map steps instead, and its zone map works the same. With the LD2412, a few things differ from an MSR-1 or MSR-2:

  • The tab has two Radar setup cards. The one under Start here checks the LD2412, and its second line starts with LD2412. The one above the zone map checks the LD2450.
  • The LD2412 has 14 gates, G0 to G13, so a calibration sets 28 thresholds.
  • LD2412 Detection Range has Distance Resolution instead of Gate Size, and Max Gate and Min Gate instead of Max Move Gate and Max Still Gate. Gates below Min Gate or beyond Max Gate are dimmed in the result table, for example G0: not used (below Min Gate 1).
  • There is no Zone Config card, and the Distances chart shows the gates and the Max Gate and Min Gate bars without live distance bars.
  • Before it writes, the calibration asks the radar for its current thresholds (Reading the radar's current thresholds...), so what it saves for Undo matches the radar.

The LD2412 also has its own background learning, Start Dynamic Background Correction on the LD2412 Controls card. It runs on the radar chip and stores its result inside the radar. Background Correction Running shows whether it is still working. Use both, in this order:

  1. Clear the room and press Start Dynamic Background Correction.
  2. Wait for Background Correction Running to turn off. Until it does, the Auto-calibrate card says Background correction is running on the LD2412. Wait for its status to turn off. and its button stays disabled.
  3. Press Calibrate with empty room with the room still empty.

Run the calibration again after any later background correction. During a calibration on an R PRO-1, the card's reminder reads Leave Radar Engineering Mode on and do not press Start Dynamic Background Correction until this finishes. Pressing it during the listen stops the calibration without changing anything.

Undo cannot reverse a background correction

The Auto-calibrate card's Undo restores the thresholds Home Assistant saved. Dynamic Background Correction changes the radar itself, outside those thresholds, so Undo cannot reverse it.

docs.title: Set the range and timeout
docs.text:
Steps 3 and 4 on Start here point at the Detection Range card: how far the radar looks, and how long presence stays on after you stop moving. Its sliders, and the ones on the two threshold cards, start locked, so a finger that lands on one while you scroll a phone can't change a setting.

  1. Press Unlock on the Sliders locked row. That unlocks this sensor's sliders on all three cards, and the row reads Sliders unlocked.

  2. Lower Max Move Gate and Max Still Gate (Max Gate on an R PRO-1) to stop the radar looking past a certain distance, such as a hallway beyond the doorway. The note under the card gives each gate's depth. On an R PRO-1, raise Min Gate to ignore anything right next to the sensor.

  3. Raise Radar Timeout if lights turn off while you sit still. It's how long Radar Target (LD2412 Presence on an R PRO-1) stays on after the radar last detects someone. It's a number box, so it's never locked.

The sliders lock again on their own after 5 minutes without a change, when you leave the tab, and each time the page loads, but never while you're dragging one. Lock on the same row locks them right away.

Touched a locked slider?

A locked slider is gray and still shows its value, and a scroll that starts on it scrolls the page. Touch one and it turns orange for a moment while Unlock flashes. Try again within 10 seconds and Home Assistant shows These sliders are locked. Press Unlock above them to change one. with an Unlock button. The lock lives in the browser page, so another phone or browser tab has its own, and Calibrate with empty room works whether the sliders are locked or not.

docs.title: Fine-tune gates by hand
docs.text:
Calibration gets most rooms right. If one spot still misbehaves, the Gate Energy chart shows you which gate to change. The outline is the signal to read: an outlined bar is a gate whose energy is above its threshold right now. Inside the range the radar uses, that means the gate is detecting a target.

  1. Press Turn on Radar Engineering Mode on the Gate Energy chart. The bars and threshold triangles appear.

  2. Leave the room and watch the chart from your phone, somewhere out of the radar's view (it can see through drywall, so step away from the wall too). A bar that is outlined while nobody is there is a gate causing false triggers. Gates outside the range the radar uses can be outlined too, but the radar ignores them: that range runs up to Max Move Gate for move bars and Max Still Gate for still bars, or from Min Gate to Max Gate on an R PRO-1.

  3. Press Unlock above the sliders, then raise the threshold of each gate causing false triggers on Move Thresholds (purple bar) or Still Thresholds (green bar) until its triangle sits a few points above the highest point the bar reaches.
  4. Sit or stand where the radar misses you. Your gate is the one whose bars rise when you shift in place; each threshold row names how far out its gate reaches, and the Gates row on the Distances chart shows it too. Lower that gate's threshold a few points at a time until its bar is outlined while you are there, but not after you leave.
  5. Turn off Radar Engineering Mode when you are done: press Turn off Radar Engineering Mode on the Radar setup card, or use the switch on the Controls card. The chart has no off button.

The Detection Range card helps too: Set the range and timeout covers it.

Calibrate first, then fine-tune

A new calibration sets every threshold again, including ones you changed by hand. If you calibrate after fine-tuning and prefer your own values, Undo brings them back.

docs.title: Draw zones on the R PRO-1 and MTR-1
docs.text:
The LD2450 radar in the R PRO-1 and MTR-1 tracks where up to three people are in the room. The zone map lets you draw areas on that map, such as the couch or the desk, and gives each area its own occupancy sensor. On an MTR-1 the tab is built around the zone map: Start here, the Radar setup card, and the map come first, with the radar's live status and controls beside them. On an R PRO-1, the LD2450's Radar setup card, the map, and the radar's live status and controls sit under the Zone Map heading, right after the first column of LD2412 cards, and its Start here card stays at the top of the tab.

The MTR-1's Start here card has three steps, and this section follows them: fix anything the Radar setup card flags, set Cone rotation to match how the sensor is mounted, then draw a zone and walk into it. An R PRO-1 without the optional LD2412 gets the same steps.

The zone map card shows your radar's name and the area the radar can see: a view cone 120 degrees wide and about 6 m (20 ft) out, with a caption at its edge such as Radar range 6 m (20 ft), 120°, and a dot for each person it tracks. The map fits that area, turned the way you set Cone rotation, plus any zone you drew outside it. Buttons sit in the bottom corners of the grid, with a row of zone buttons and a Configure section underneath.

The map is in feet when Home Assistant uses US customary units (Settings → System → General), and in meters otherwise. The m / ft switch in the bottom-right corner of the map changes it. When an administrator presses it, the choice is saved for that radar, so everyone who opens its map sees that unit. Anyone else changes only their own view, until they reload the page. Zones are stored in millimeters either way, so switching units never moves a zone.

docs.title: Check the LD2450's Radar setup card
docs.text:
The Radar setup card right above the map checks the two LD2450 settings that decide whether the map can show people. The radar chip keeps these itself, and Apollo firmware never sets them:

  • Zone Type should be Disabled, because the zone map replaces the radar's own built-in zones. On Detection, the radar reports only people inside those built-in zones, and with none set it reports nobody, so the map stays empty. On Filter, it hides people inside them.
  • Multi Target Tracking should be on. Off, the radar tracks only one person.

Press the button the card shows: Set Zone Type to Disabled, Turn on Multi Target Tracking, or Use recommended settings when both need fixing. The card changes nothing until you press one, and reads Radar settings look good. once both are right. On an R PRO-1, Home Assistant hides Multi Target Tracking by default, so the card checks only Zone Type until you enable that setting (see The zone map shows nobody, or only one person).

docs.title: Match the map to how the sensor is mounted
docs.text:
Turn the map so its view cone points the way your sensor faces. The tracked dots turn with it.

  1. Open Configure under the grid.
  2. If the Cone rotation: slider is gray, the map is locked: press Locked on the map first (see Lock and unlock).
  3. Drag Cone rotation: (from -180° to 180°) until the view cone points the way your sensor faces. When you let go, the angle is saved for the radar and the map fits the turned cone. Double-click the slider to reset it.

docs.title: Lock and unlock
docs.text:
The bottom-right corner has a lock toggle that reads Unlocked (🔓) or Locked (🔒). The map starts locked once the radar has zones, and your browser remembers your choice for each radar. A radar with no zones yet starts unlocked, so you can set Cone rotation and draw right away. While the map is locked:

  • Drawing on it shows Unlock the grid before drawing.
  • The Cone rotation slider is gray, and a scroll that starts on it scrolls the page. A tap or drag on it outlines Locked and shows Cone rotation is locked. Press Locked on the map to change it.
  • Clear All Zones, double-clicking a zone's button, ↶ (Undo last zone change), and Configure → Zones still change your zones.

On a phone or tablet, the grid takes every touch, so a swipe on it doesn't scroll the page, even while the map is locked. Scroll with your finger outside the grid, for example on the radar's name above it. Stay off the zone buttons while you scroll: a stray tap on Clear All Zones clears every zone's shape. Keep the map on Locked when you're not drawing: on an unlocked map, a swipe across the grid can draw a new shape for the selected zone and replace its old one.

From Apollo mmWave 2.2.6, only administrators can save zone changes. Other users still see the zones and their presence sensors, and a change they try to make shows a Could not save message.

docs.title: Add a zone
docs.text: Open Configure → Zones and press Add Zone. The new zone is named Zone 1 (then Zone 2, and so on), gets its own button under the grid, and is selected and ready to draw.

docs.title: Draw a zone
docs.text:
You draw each zone on the grid as a rectangle, ellipse, or polygon.

  1. Unlock the map and press the zone's button to select it.
  2. Press ✎ (Drawing modes) in the bottom-left corner and pick a shape: ▭ (Rectangle), ◯ (Ellipse), or ⬠ (Polygon).
  3. For a rectangle or ellipse, drag across the grid and let go to save.
  4. For a polygon, click each corner, then double-click or press ✓ (Finish polygon) to save. A polygon can have up to 32 points. ↺ (Undo last point) or Backspace removes the last point, and Esc cancels the shape.

Drawing a new shape for a zone replaces its old one. Made a mistake? ↶ (Undo last zone change) in the bottom-right corner puts the last change back. Drawing works with touch too, so you can draw zones from a phone or tablet.

docs.title: Rename a zone
docs.text: In Configure → Zones, type a new name next to the zone and press Save. The name appears on the zone's button.

docs.title: Clear or delete a zone
docs.text: Double-click a zone's button to clear its shape, or press Clear All Zones to clear every shape while keeping the zones. To remove a zone completely, along with its sensors, press Delete next to it in Configure → Zones.

docs.title: Use the zone sensors
docs.text:
Each zone gets an occupancy sensor named Zone 1 presence (and so on) on the radar's device page in Home Assistant. It turns on when a tracked person is inside the zone, ready to use in your automations. When you rename a zone on the card, its sensors follow, so a zone named Couch gets Zone 1 presence - Couch. A name you gave the sensor yourself in Home Assistant is kept.

To try a zone, reload the page after you draw it, then walk into it. The Zone presence card next to the map lists each zone's sensor and colors it while someone is in the zone, and Occupancy History adds a line for the zone, covering the last 24 hours.

Under it, LD2450 Live shows what the radar reports right now. If the map shows no dot with you in the room, look here first: Presence off means the radar itself reports nobody.

LD2450 Controls holds Zone Type, Multi Target Tracking, Radar Timeout, Radar Bluetooth (HLK app), Restart Radar, and Factory Reset Radar, whichever your sensor has (the MTR-1 has no Restart Radar). The restart and the reset ask before they act. Radar Timeout is how long LD2450 Presence stays on after the radar last sees someone. It doesn't hold the zones you draw: a zone turns off as soon as nobody is in it. While Zone Type isn't Disabled, a Radar's built-in zones card shows the radar chip's own zones, which are not the zones on the map.

While the radar is offline, or still reconnecting after a restart, zone presence reads off, not unavailable. An automation that waits for a zone to be clear for some minutes can't tell that apart from an empty zone, so have it also check that the radar itself is online.

docs.title: Calibrate from an automation
docs.text:
The Calibrate with empty room button runs the apollo_mmwave.calibrate_gates action, and your automations can run it too. When an automation already knows the room is empty, set settle_s: 0 to skip the countdown, and wait: true to get the result back when the run ends. This example recalibrates an office radar at 3:00 AM if nobody has been detected for 30 minutes, and sends a notification when the outcome is anything other than applied:

alias: Recalibrate the office radar overnight
triggers:
  - trigger: time
    at: "03:00:00"
conditions:
  - condition: state
    entity_id: binary_sensor.apollo_msr_2_abc123_radar_target
    state: "off"
    for: "00:30:00"
actions:
  - action: apollo_mmwave.calibrate_gates
    data:
      device_id: your_device_id
      settle_s: 0
      wait: true
    response_variable: calibration
  - if:
      - condition: template
        value_template: "{{ calibration.outcome != 'applied' }}"
    then:
      - action: persistent_notification.create
        data:
          title: Radar calibration
          message: >
            Outcome {{ calibration.outcome }}
            {% if calibration.error %}({{ calibration.error.message }}){% endif %},
            {{ calibration.changed }} thresholds changed.

To use it, create a new automation under Settings → Automations & scenes, open the three-dot menu, choose Edit in YAML, and paste it in. Then replace binary_sensor.apollo_msr_2_abc123_radar_target with your radar's Radar Target sensor, and your_device_id with your radar. To fill in the device without looking up its ID, switch the action to the visual editor and pick your radar under Radar Device. If the action is refused before it starts (the radar is offline, for example), the automation stops with an error at that step instead of sending the notification.

Each call calibrates one radar. Two related actions round it out: apollo_mmwave.cancel_calibration stops a running job, and apollo_mmwave.restore_gate_thresholds does what Undo does. The card offers only the newest saved thresholds, while the action can restore an older set with its snapshot_id field. Settings → Tools → Actions lists every field, and the button below opens it with apollo_mmwave.calibrate_gates selected.

Only automate it for a room you know is empty

A person sleeping or a pet napping can look like an empty room to an automation. Pick a time and a room where nobody is, and remember each run replaces any thresholds you set by hand.

docs.title: The radar still triggers with nobody there
docs.text:
A calibration sets each threshold a margin above the highest energy it heard during a one-minute listen. Something that moves now and then, like a fan that cycles or the heating coming on, may not have moved during that minute.

  1. Update Apollo mmWave to 2.2.4 or newer and press Calibrate with empty room again. 2.2.4 leaves more headroom above the room's noise (15 points instead of 10).
  2. Calibrate while whatever usually runs in the room is running: the fan on, the heating or air conditioning cycling. If it only comes on now and then, listen for longer so a cycle falls inside the listen, for example 5 minutes (duration_s: 300, set the same way as margin in step 3).

  3. Still too sensitive? Raise margin, the points added above each gate's peak, for example to 20 or 25, and calibrate again. It sets the headroom on most gates. The percentage (margin_pct) only takes over on gates whose peak is 43 or more at the defaults, such as gates right at the sensor, so raising it changes little in most rooms. There are two places to set it:

    • For one run, on any dashboard: open Settings → Tools → Actions, pick Calibrate gate thresholds (empty room), choose your radar under Radar Device, tick Headroom (points) and set it to 20 (and Listen for (seconds) for a longer listen), then press Perform action and leave the room. The Auto-calibrate card shows the run as it goes.

    • For every run, on your own dashboard: add a calibration block to the Auto-calibrate card's YAML. Calibrate with empty room then uses it each time:

      type: custom:apollo-radar-calibrate-card
device_id: your_device_id
calibration:
  margin: 20
  duration_s: 300

      The keys go under calibration:. Typed at the card's top level, they are ignored. On the Apollo mmWave dashboard, the same block can go under strategy: in its raw configuration; the Apollo mmWave configuration guide has the details.

  4. If only one spot misbehaves, raise only that gate's threshold, as described in Fine-tune gates by hand.

If the radar now misses you instead, press Undo (restore your previous values), or calibrate again with a smaller margin.

docs.title: Calibration will not start
docs.text:
The Calibrate with empty room button is disabled when the card cannot run a calibration. The card says why:

  • Radar is offline. Calibration needs the radar online and its gate entities enabled. Check that the radar is powered and shows as online under Settings → Devices & services → ESPHome. If it is online, open your sensor's device page from that list and check that the Radar Engineering Mode switch and the gate threshold and gate energy entities are enabled. A disabled entity is listed under + N entities not shown: select it, open its settings (the cog), turn on Enabled, and click Update.

  • Background correction is running on the LD2412. Wait for its status to turn off. (R PRO-1) Wait for Background Correction Running to turn off.

  • Apollo mmWave is still loading... The integration is starting or reloading, and the card keeps trying on its own. If it changes to Apollo mmWave is not loaded, so calibration is unavailable., press Retry. If that keeps happening, check Settings → Devices & services for an error on the Apollo mmWave integration.

If the button works but the card answers with a line starting Calibration failed:, the rest of the line says what went wrong, and Try again runs it again once you have fixed it. The common ones:

  • The radar is unavailable right now. Check that it is online, then try again. The radar dropped off the network.
  • Home Assistant could not turn Radar Engineering Mode on within 10 s. Is the radar online? The radar did not respond to the switch.
  • No gate energy readings arrived within 20 s of turning Radar Engineering Mode on. Check that the radar is online and that Radar Engineering Mode on the Controls card brings the Gate Energy chart to life.
  • Radar Engineering Mode turned off during the listen. Nothing was changed. Someone, or an automation, turned it off during the listen. Leave it on and try again.
  • The radar has not reported 18 of its threshold values yet. The number is how many are missing: up to 18 on an MSR-1 or MSR-2, and up to 28 on an R PRO-1. The radar has not sent its thresholds to Home Assistant since it started, which can happen after it has been running for a long time. Press Read settings from the radar (the Radar setup card at the top of the tab offers it too): the card asks the radar for its settings, shows Reading settings from the radar..., and tries again a few seconds later. If the card can't find the radar's query params button, it says Open the radar's device page, press its Query Params button in the Diagnostic section, wait a few seconds, then try again.
  • Your Home Assistant user is not allowed to control this radar's entities. Run the calibration from a Home Assistant user that can control the radar.

On an R PRO-1 without the LD2412 addon, there's no radar behind the LD2412 cards, so the Auto-calibrate card can't calibrate. Depending on what the sensor reports, the card either reads Radar is offline. Calibration needs the radar online and its gate entities enabled. with its buttons disabled, or answers Calibrate with empty room with The radar has not reported 28 of its threshold values yet. Reading the settings from the radar can't fix either one. Skip the calibration: the zone map is what that sensor uses.

docs.title: Radar Engineering Mode was left on
docs.text:
The calibration only turns Radar Engineering Mode off if it was the one that turned it on. If you turned it on yourself, or with the button on the Gate Energy chart, it stays on until you turn it off. The Radar setup card at the top of the tab says so while it's on: press its Turn off Radar Engineering Mode button, or use the Radar Engineering Mode switch on the Controls card.

If Home Assistant restarted during the countdown or the listen, nothing was written: the calibration turns Radar Engineering Mode back off when Home Assistant starts again, and the card says, for example, Last calibration Oct 12, 12:37 AM was stopped by a Home Assistant restart. Nothing was changed. Press Calibrate with empty room to run it again.

If Home Assistant restarted while thresholds were being written, or the radar went offline before the calibration could turn the mode off, the Auto-calibrate card shows a banner the next time you open it. It starts with A calibration was interrupted by a restart. or The last calibration could not turn Radar Engineering Mode back off (the radar was offline). Press Turn it off next to Radar Engineering Mode may still be on. If the banner also says Some thresholds may have been written., press its Undo to put the saved thresholds back, then run the calibration again.

Keep Radar Engineering Mode out of your history

While Radar Engineering Mode is on, the radar updates its 18 (MSR-1 and MSR-2) or 28 (R PRO-1) gate energy sensors about once a second, and Home Assistant's recorder, the part that saves history, stores every update. Turning the mode off when you're done avoids this. If you like to leave it on to watch the chart, add the block below to your configuration.yaml (the File editor app is one way to open it), then restart Home Assistant. If the file already has a recorder: section, add the exclude: lines to it instead of adding a second recorder: key.

configuration.yaml
recorder:
  exclude:
    entity_globs:
      - sensor.*_g?_move_energy     # LD2410: g0 to g8
      - sensor.*_g?_still_energy
      - sensor.*_g??_move_energy    # LD2412: g00 to g13
      - sensor.*_g??_still_energy

docs.title: Thresholds did not change on the radar
docs.text:
• You ran a preview. Preview only never writes anything. Press Calibrate and apply, or Calibrate with empty room.
  • The new value matched the old one. Cells that read (unchanged) were already right, so nothing was written.
  • The gate had no data. Gates marked no data keep their old thresholds. Check the radar's connection and run the calibration again.
  • The radar did not confirm the value. Cells marked (not confirmed) and the warning that values could not be confirmed mean the radar did not report the new value back. Check the gates on the Move Thresholds and Still Thresholds cards, then run it again once the radar is stable, or set those gates by hand.
  • The run was stopped. Stopped. Nothing was changed. means nothing was written.

docs.title: The chart says to turn on Radar Engineering Mode
docs.text:
If the chart instead reads Radar unavailable and Waiting for the device to reconnect, the radar is offline and the button is hidden until it comes back: check its power and Wi-Fi. Otherwise, the Gate Energy chart only shows bars while Radar Engineering Mode is on. Press Turn on Radar Engineering Mode on the chart itself, or turn on Radar Engineering Mode on the Controls card. The bars appear within a few seconds, once the radar starts sending energy. If the calibration turned the mode on, it turns it back off when it finishes, so the overlay returning after a calibration is expected.

Prefer the radar maker's app?

The HLKRadarTool app connects over the radar's Bluetooth (the Radar Bluetooth (HLK app) row on the Controls card, or on LD2450 Controls for the LD2450) and has its own auto-calibration. Each sensor has its own guide: MSR-1, MSR-2, R PRO-1, and MTR-1.

docs.title: The zone map shows nobody, or only one person
docs.text:
Start with the LD2450's Radar setup card, right above the map.

No dot at all. The usual cause is Zone Type set to Detection: the radar then reports only people inside its own built-in zones, and with none set it reports nobody. Press Set Zone Type to Disabled, or Use recommended settings if the card shows that instead. If Zone Type is already Disabled and Presence on the LD2450 Live card stays off with you in front of the sensor, the radar itself sees nobody: check that it's online and facing the room.

One dot with several people in the room. Usually Multi Target Tracking is off. Press Turn on Multi Target Tracking (or Use recommended settings if the card shows that instead) on the Radar setup card. On an R PRO-1, Home Assistant hides that setting by default, so the card can't check it and shows no button. Enable it once:

  1. Open the sensor's device page with All settings for this device → on the Start here card.
  2. Under Configuration, open the entities that aren't shown and select LD2450 Multi Target Tracking.
  3. Open its settings (⚙), turn on Enabled, and select Update.
  4. Reload the dashboard after a minute. The Radar setup card then checks the setting and offers its button when it's off.

docs.title: The dots sit at the sensor, or a zone misses you
docs.text:
Apollo mmWave 2.2.7 fixed this. Before it, when Home Assistant used US customary units (or you changed a Target X or Target Y sensor's unit), the zone map read the radar's positions in inches as if they were millimeters. The dots sat at or right around the sensor, and zone presence didn't turn on. Update Apollo mmWave (see Upgrade from an older setup) and the dots land where people are.

A zone you drew while the dots were in the wrong place may not cover where people show up now. Walk through the room, watch the dots, and redraw any zone that's off.

docs.title: A slider won't move
docs.text: The sliders on Detection Range, Move Thresholds, and Still Thresholds start locked. Press Unlock on the Sliders locked row above them (see Set the range and timeout). The Cone rotation slider on the zone map locks with the map: press Locked on the map first.

docs.title: Send Apollo a support file
docs.text:
Still stuck? Send Apollo a support file with your question. It holds the Apollo mmWave and Home Assistant versions, the dashboard's state, and each radar's model, firmware, settings, zones, and last calibration. It leaves out MAC and IP addresses, Wi-Fi network names, and tokens, and downloading it changes nothing. Only administrators can download it.

  1. Go to Settings → Devices & services and open Apollo mmWave. The Device card at the bottom of each tab links there too.

  2. Open the three-dot menu and choose Download diagnostics.

  3. Attach the file to your message to Apollo support, or to your issue on GitHub.

Check the file before you post it publicly

The file includes your zones and their names, which can show the layout of your home. Send it to Apollo support, or look through it before you attach it to a public GitHub issue.

docs.title: R PRO-1 Zone Mapper tool
docs.text:
The Apollo R PRO-1's LD2450 mmWave sensor tracks up to three targets across the room. With the Zone Mapper tool you draw its detection zones on a visual grid in Home Assistant, watch targets move in real time, and get an occupancy sensor for every zone you draw.

Using the Apollo mmWave integration?

Its dashboard has a zone map built in, with a tab for each MTR-1 and R PRO-1, so you don't need Zone Mapper as well. See Draw zones on the R PRO-1 and MTR-1. Either way, leave the radar's Zone Type (LD2450 Zone Type on an R PRO-1) on Disabled. On Detection, the radar reports only people inside its own built-in zones, and with none set it reports nobody.

Zone Mapper has two parts that work together:

  • The Zone Mapper integration, a backend that stores your zones and creates an occupancy sensor for each one.
  • The Zone Mapper card, a dashboard card where you draw and manage the zones.

Install both parts

The card does nothing without the integration, and the integration has no interface without the card. Complete both installations before you start drawing zones. Home Assistant 2025.9.4 or newer is recommended.

docs.title: Video walkthrough
docs.text: MostlyChris covers the full setup, from installation to drawing your first zones:

docs.title: Install with HACS (recommended)
docs.text:
HACS is a community store for Home Assistant that handles installing and updating custom integrations and cards. If you don't have it yet, follow the HACS download guide and initial configuration guide.

With HACS in place, both Zone Mapper parts install in one pass. The two buttons under step 1 cover steps 1 to 5: the first opens the integration and the second opens the card. Each one adds its repository, after HACS asks you to confirm, and opens it so you can click Download right there. Use both, then go on at step 6.

  1. Open HACS from your Home Assistant sidebar.

  2. Click the three-dot menu in the upper right corner and choose Custom repositories.

  3. Add https://github.com/ApolloAutomation/zone-mapper with type Integration.
  4. Add https://github.com/ApolloAutomation/zone-mapper-card with type Dashboard.
  5. Search HACS for Zone Mapper and download both the integration and the card.
  6. Restart Home Assistant when prompted.

  7. Go to Settings → Devices & services → Add integration, search for Zone Mapper, and add it.

The integration adds a "Zone Mapper" view with the card to your default dashboard the first time it is set up, so you don't have to place the card yourself (storage-mode dashboards only; you can opt out in the integration options). Open the new view and you're ready to pick your device and start drawing.

docs.title: Manual installation
docs.text:
If you'd rather install without HACS:

  1. Copy the contents of the integration's custom_components folder to /config/custom_components/zone_mapper.
  2. Download zone-mapper-card.js from the card repository to /config/www.

  3. Add the card as a resource under Settings → Dashboards → Resources with URL /local/zone-mapper-card.js and type JavaScript Module.

  4. Restart Home Assistant, then hard-refresh your browser to clear the cached resource list.

docs.title: Configure the card
docs.text:
Zones themselves are managed on the card, so the YAML stays small: it sets the location name, theme, grid size, and units.

type: custom:zone-mapper-card
location: Office       # shown on the card and used to build zone entity IDs
dark_mode: false
start_locked: true     # start with drawing locked

# Units (display only, stored as mm internally)
input_units: mm        # mm | cm | m | in | ft
grid_units: mm         # mm | cm | m | in | ft
unit_display: false    # show unit-aware axis labels and cone range rings
unit_label_size: 18    # optional, px (8..24)

# Grid extents (Y points down: y_min is the top edge, y_max is the bottom)
grid:
  x_min: -6000
  x_max: 6000
  y_min: 0
  y_max: 12000

# Device view cone
device_cone:
  y_max: 6000          # max range (radius) to display
  fov_deg: 120         # total horizontal field of view (120 shows ±60°)
  angle_deg: 0         # initial rotation (-180..180)

docs.title: Set target entities
docs.text:
The card needs to know which X/Y coordinate sensors to track:

  1. Click the Configure drop-down, then Device and Targets.
  2. Select your device. The X/Y target entities populate automatically, and you can adjust them by hand if needed.
  3. For helper entities that aren't tied to a device, leave the device picker on Select device and use Add X/Y Pair instead.
  4. Click Apply to save your selection.

Using the imperial system? Switch your target sensors to millimeters

Home Assistant shows the Target X and Y sensors in inches (in) when your system uses US units, while the card reads them in millimeters (mm). When the units don't match, your target dots never appear on the grid. Metric users can skip this; everyone else, convert the sensors before drawing zones:

  1. Open your device's page under Settings → Devices & services → ESPHome.

  2. Under Sensors, click Target 1 X, open its settings with the gear icon, and change Unit of Measurement to mm.

  3. Repeat for the X and Y sensors of all three targets (six entities in total).

Changing the card's units instead also works, but then you need to adjust the grid distances to match, so converting the sensors is the recommended path.

docs.title: Add zones
docs.text:
1. Click the Configure drop-down, then Zones.
  2. Click Add Zone, name the zone, and click Save.

Zones and their paired entities can be deleted from the same panel.

docs.title: Draw zones
docs.text:
This is where the tool earns its "best" rating: instead of typing coordinates, you draw the zone where you want it.

  1. Select a zone with its button.
  2. Click ✎ and choose a shape: rectangle, ellipse, or polygon.
  3. For rectangles and ellipses, drag to define the bounding box and release to save.
  4. For polygons, click to place vertices and double-click to finish. Backspace removes the last vertex, and Esc cancels the in-progress shape.

A few controls worth knowing:

  • Double-click a zone's button to clear that zone.
  • Toggle 🔒 to lock the card and prevent accidental edits.
  • Rotate the device's view cone with the slider to match how the sensor is mounted. Target dots rotate with it, and the angle persists across restarts.
  • Drawing works with touch as well as a mouse, so you can set up zones from a phone or tablet.

docs.title: Entities created
docs.text:
For each zone, the integration creates:

  • A coordinate sensor, sensor.zone_mapper_<location>_zone_<id>, that stores the zone's shape so it survives restarts.
  • A presence binary sensor, <location> Zone <id> Presence, that turns on when any tracked target is inside the zone.

The location is slugified with Home Assistant's rules, so location: Office produces sensor.zone_mapper_office_zone_1. Entities are created the first time you draw a zone for a location.

docs.title: Example automation
docs.text:
The presence sensors work like any other occupancy sensor. This automation turns on a light when zone 1 is occupied, then turns it off two minutes after the zone empties:

alias: Office Light Control
mode: restart
max_exceeded: silent
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: binary_sensor.office_zone_1_presence
    from: "off"
    to: "on"
actions:
  - alias: Turn on the light
    action: light.turn_on
    target:
      entity_id: light.office_1
  - alias: Wait until the zone is empty
    wait_for_trigger:
      trigger: state
      entity_id: binary_sensor.office_zone_1_presence
      from: "on"
      to: "off"
  - alias: Wait two minutes
    delay: 120
  - alias: Turn off the light
    action: light.turn_off
    target:
      entity_id: light.office_1

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Click Apply and Save after setting up the card or making changes. Most "nothing happens" reports come down to a missed Apply.
  • Resource not found: confirm the resource URL is /local/zone-mapper-card.js, the file is under /config/www, and clear your browser cache.

  • Zones don't persist: check the coordinate sensor's attributes for shape, data, and rotation_deg under Developer Tools → States (Settings → Tools → States in Home Assistant 2026.8 and newer), and confirm the zone_mapper.update_zone service is being called.

  • Coordinate entity not found: draw a zone once to create the entities for that location.

  • No target dots appear when you move: your Target X/Y sensors are most likely reporting in inches while the card reads millimeters. Switch the six target sensors to mm as described under Set target entities.
  • Presence never turns on: verify the tracked X/Y entities have numeric states (not unknown or unavailable) and that the target actually sits inside the drawn zone.
  • Target dots linger after you leave the room: a known quirk of many LD2450 sensors running ESPHome, not a Zone Mapper issue.

docs.title: Going deeper
docs.text: Zone Mapper supports more than this page covers, including a zone_mapper.update_zone service for scripted zone changes, pre-seeded zone lists, and multi-unit grids. The README files in the zone-mapper and zone-mapper-card repositories document the full service contract and card options.

docs.title: Light sensor (LTR-390UV)
docs.text:
The R PRO-1 doesn't have any slits on the front of the case, so UV rays can't directly reach the sensor for UV detection. However, light can still enter from around the edges or behind the front panel, allowing the lux readings to spike when ambient light is present.

The RGB LED will trigger the Light sensor!

Make sure that your automations do not interfere with each other. This includes being aware that your onboard LED can trigger the lux reading but not the uv reading of the LTR390 in your device.

docs.title: Wall mounting
docs.text: The R PRO-1 should be mounted 1.5-2 meters off the ground which will then provide a nice even 120 degree FOV for the LD2450 and 150 degree FOV for the LD2412.

docs.title: Ceiling mounting
docs.text:
The R PRO-1 should be mounted 2.6-3 meters (8-10 feet) high when mounted on the ceiling using our ceiling mount kit.

There are actually two sensors in your R PRO-1 if you bought the optional LD2412 addon!

The multi-target LD2450:

  • The horizontal FOV angle is -60 to 60 degrees (120 degrees total).
  • The vertical FOV angle is -35 to 35 degrees (70 degrees total).
  • Zones are X and Y coordinate zones and are user-configurable.

Helpful hints for LD2450 Zones:

  • The X axis is where you can get tripped up, especially when both values are negative: -3456 is less than -2345.
  • X1 must always be less than X2, and Y1 must always be less than Y2.
  • The Y axis is easier since it's never negative.
  • The Plotly chart will still render the rectangles even if the X1/X2 and Y1/Y2 values are reversed.
  • The zones cannot overlap.

The single-target LD2412:

  • The horizontal FOV angle is -75 to 75 degrees (150 degrees total).
  • The vertical FOV angle is -35 to 35 degrees (70 degrees total).
  • Gates are pre-defined by the radar module and are in 0.75 meter increments.

docs.title: Sensor definitions
docs.text:
Once added to Home Assistant you can configure different settings for your R PRO-1. Use the tabs below to see what each entity does, grouped the same way Home Assistant displays them.

The R PRO-1 pairs two radars: an LD2450 that tracks the position of up to three targets and reports zone occupancy, and an LD2412 that handles presence and per-gate sensitivity tuning. It also carries an LTR390 light sensor and an optional SCD40 CO₂ module.

How often readings update

The Default Update column is how often each entity refreshes. Radar entities update in real time as targets move. The SCD40 and LTR390 sensors report every 60s.

ControlsSensorsConfigurationDiagnostic Control What it does RGB Light Four RGB Neopixel LEDs. Click the light bulb or color wheel to change the color. Use the toggle to turn them on or off. Calibrate SCD40 To 420ppm Forces a fresh-air calibration of the SCD40 CO₂ sensor to the outdoor baseline (about 420 ppm). Run it outdoors or next to an open window. Only needed when CO2 Auto Calibration is off. Entity Default Update What it shows Apollo Firmware Version on boot The Apollo firmware build installed on the device (for example, 26.3.2.1). ESPHome Version on boot The ESPHome version the firmware was compiled with. Firmware Update — Shows whether a firmware update is available and lets you update from inside Home Assistant. IP Address on connect The device's IP address on your network (Wi-Fi firmware). Online on change Connection status of the device to Home Assistant. ESP Temperature 60s Internal temperature of the ESP32 chip. Runs warmer than the room because of the processor and Wi-Fi radio. Disabled by default. Uptime 60s How long the device has been running since its last reboot. LD2412 Dynamic Background Correction Status real-time Whether the LD2412 is running dynamic background correction. LD2412 Out Pin real-time State of the LD2412 hardware output pin. Disabled by default. LD2412 Firmware on boot Firmware version installed on the LD2412 radar module. Disabled by default. LD2412 BT MAC on boot Bluetooth MAC address of the LD2412 radar module. Disabled by default. LD2412 g00 to g13 move energy real-time Live move energy for each gate (g00 to g13), used when tuning with Engineering Mode. LD2412 g00 to g13 still energy real-time Live still energy for each gate (g00 to g13), used when tuning with Engineering Mode. LD2412 Query params — Queries the LD2412's current parameters for debugging or advanced setup. LD2412 Restart — Restarts the LD2412 radar module. LD2412 Start Dynamic Background Correction — Kicks off a dynamic background correction pass on the LD2412. LD2450 Firmware on boot Firmware version installed on the LD2450 radar module. Disabled by default. LD2450 BT MAC on boot Bluetooth MAC address of the LD2450 radar module. Disabled by default. LD2450 Restart — Restarts the LD2450 radar module.

Join our Discord if you need more help!

docs.title: Air quality & light
docs.text: Sensor Default Update Details CO2 60s True NDIR reading from the SCD40. Shows Unknown if you do not have the CO₂ module. You can re-calibrate it to the outdoor baseline. SCD40 Temperature 60s Temperature from the optional SCD40 module. Disabled by default. Adjusted by the SCD40 Temperature Offset. SCD40 Humidity 60s Humidity from the optional SCD40 module. Disabled by default. Adjusted by the SCD40 Humidity Offset. LTR390 Light 60s Ambient light level in lux from the LTR390. LTR390 UV Index 60s UV index measured by the LTR390.

docs.title: Combined presence
docs.text: Sensor Default Update Details Combined Presence real-time Combined occupancy: shows Detected when either the LD2450 or the LD2412 radar sees a target, and Clear when neither does. Use this entity for automations and dashboards instead of the individual radar presence sensors.

docs.title: Radar presence (LD2412 mmWave)
docs.text: Sensor Default Update Details LD2412 Presence real-time Whether the LD2412 detects any target, moving or still. LD2412 Moving Target real-time Whether the LD2412 detects only a moving target. LD2412 Still Target real-time Whether the LD2412 detects only a still target. LD2412 Detection Distance real-time Distance of the target being tracked. Disabled by default. LD2412 Moving Distance real-time Distance of the moving target being tracked. Disabled by default. LD2412 Still Distance real-time Distance of the still target being tracked. Disabled by default. LD2412 Move Energy real-time Energy level of the moving target being tracked. Disabled by default. LD2412 Still Energy real-time Energy level of the still target being tracked. Disabled by default. LD2412 Light real-time Light level reported by the LD2412. Disabled by default.

docs.title: Radar tracking (LD2450 mmWave)
docs.text: Sensor Default Update Details LD2450 Presence real-time Whether the radar currently detects any target. Great for occupancy automations. LD2450 Moving Target real-time Whether a moving target is detected. LD2450 Still Target real-time Whether a stationary target is detected. LD2450 Presence Target Count real-time Count of all presence targets (max 3). LD2450 Moving Target Count real-time Count of all moving targets (max 3). LD2450 Still Target Count real-time Count of all still targets (max 3). LD2450 Target-1 / Target-2 / Target-3 X real-time Distance in mm of the target from the sensor along the X-axis (negative = left, positive = right, range -3000 to 3000). LD2450 Target-1 / Target-2 / Target-3 Y real-time Distance in mm of the target from the sensor in the Y direction (near/far, range 0 to 6000). LD2450 Target-1 / Target-2 / Target-3 Speed real-time Speed of the moving target in mm/s. LD2450 Target-1 / Target-2 / Target-3 Angle real-time Angle of the target in degrees relative to the sensor. LD2450 Target-1 / Target-2 / Target-3 Distance real-time Straight-line distance of the target from the sensor. LD2450 Target-1 / Target-2 / Target-3 Resolution real-time Target detection range resolution in mm. Disabled by default. LD2450 Target-1 / Target-2 / Target-3 Direction real-time Direction of the target: Stationary, Moving away, Approaching, or NA. LD2450 Zone-1 / Zone-2 / Zone-3 All Target Count real-time Total targets in the zone, stationary or moving. LD2450 Zone-1 / Zone-2 / Zone-3 Moving Target Count real-time Count of moving targets in the zone. LD2450 Zone-1 / Zone-2 / Zone-3 Still Target Count real-time Count of stationary targets in the zone.

docs.title: General
docs.text: Setting Default What it does ESP Reboot — Restarts the device. Helpful for troubleshooting or refreshing the connection. Firmware Type WiFi / Ethernet Switches between the Wi-Fi and Ethernet firmware without re-flashing. After picking the firmware you want, press Firmware Update to apply it. Reduce DB Reporting Off Filters several entities so they only report when a threshold is met, using less Wi-Fi airtime and less Home Assistant database space. SCD40 Temperature Offset 18.86 °C Calibration offset for the SCD40 temperature reading. Disabled by default. SCD40 Humidity Offset 0 % Calibration offset for the SCD40 humidity reading. Disabled by default. CO2 Auto Calibration On Keeps the SCD40 CO₂ sensor calibrated automatically. The sensor assumes it sees fresh air (about 420 ppm) at least once a week and corrects its baseline to match. Turn it off if the device sits in a space that rarely gets fresh air, then calibrate manually with Calibrate SCD40 To 420ppm every 1 to 2 years.

docs.title: LD2412 radar
docs.text: Setting Default What it does LD2412 Bluetooth — Toggles the LD2412's Bluetooth so you can connect with the HLK Radartool phone app for tuning. Turn it back off when finished. LD2412 Engineering Mode — Enables the g00 to g13 move and still energy readouts used for mmWave tuning. LD2412 Timeout — Seconds the LD2412 presence stays detected after the target is lost. LD2412 min distance gate — Minimum distance gate for detection. LD2412 max distance gate — Maximum distance gate for detection. LD2412 g00 to g13 move threshold — Movement sensitivity threshold for each 0.75 m gate, from gate 0 (nearest) to gate 13. Raise a gate's value to tune out false motion at that distance. LD2412 g00 to g13 still threshold — Stillness sensitivity threshold for each 0.75 m gate, from gate 0 (nearest) to gate 13. LD2412 Factory Reset — Restores the LD2412's move and still thresholds to the manufacturer defaults. LD2412 Light Threshold — Light level threshold for the LD2412. Disabled by default. LD2412 Light Function — Selects how the LD2412 uses its light reading. Disabled by default. LD2412 Hardware output pin level — Output pin level for the LD2412. Disabled by default. LD2412 Distance resolution — Distance resolution for the LD2412. Disabled by default. LD2412 baud rate from module Serial baud rate the LD2412 uses to talk to the R PRO-1 (default 115200). Disabled by default; no need to change.

docs.title: LD2450 radar
docs.text: Setting Default What it does LD2450 Bluetooth — Toggles the LD2450's Bluetooth so you can connect with the HLK Radartool phone app for tuning. Turn it back off when finished. LD2450 Multi Target Tracking from module Turns multi-target tracking on or off. Initial state is read from the LD2450 at boot. Disabled by default. LD2450 Timeout — Seconds the LD2450 presence stays detected after the target is lost. LD2450 Zone Type Disabled Zone detection mode: Disabled, Detection (only detect targets inside the zone), or Filter (exclude the zone from detection). With Detection and no zones set, the radar detects nobody, so keep Disabled unless you use the radar's own zones. LD2450 Zone-1 / Zone-2 / Zone-3 X1, X2 — Start and end X coordinates of the zone in mm (-4860 left to 4860 right). LD2450 Zone-1 / Zone-2 / Zone-3 Y1, Y2 — Start and end Y coordinates of the zone in mm (0 to 7560). LD2450 Factory Reset — Resets the LD2450 radar module to its factory settings. LD2450 Baud rate from module Serial baud rate the LD2450 uses to talk to the R PRO-1 (default 256000). Disabled by default; no need to change.

docs.title: Firmware switching guide
docs.text:
R PRO-1 ships with Wi-Fi firmware because some people might not have ethernet or PoE.

Your device needs to be able to connect to the internet to switch between firmware files. If you are connecting to an IoT network on a subnet/vlan unable to access github.com then this will not work. You can also manually reflash your device serially (usb) by following our flashing guide!

docs.title: Switch to Ethernet
docs.text:
Follow these steps to switch your R PRO-1 from the Wi-Fi firmware to the Ethernet firmware.

1. Navigate to the ESPHome integration by going to settings -> ESPHome integration -> click on "1 device" below your Apollo R PRO-1.

2. Scroll down until you see the "Firmware Type" dropdown and select "Ethernet".

3. Locate the Firmware Update entity and click on "PRESS".

4. Wait a few minutes. This will download the new firmware file from our GitHub repo and then install the image.

5. Your device is now on the Ethernet firmware and is ready to configure!

docs.title: Switch to Wi-Fi
docs.text:
Follow these steps to switch your R PRO-1 from the Ethernet firmware back to the Wi-Fi firmware.

1. Navigate to the ESPHome integration by going to settings -> ESPHome integration -> click on "1 device" below your Apollo R PRO-1.

2. Scroll down until you see the "Firmware Type" dropdown and select "WiFi".

3. Locate the Firmware Update entity and click on "PRESS".

4. Wait a few minutes. This will download the new firmware file from our GitHub repo and then install the image.

Head to the getting started docs to get your sensor integrated with Home Assistant!

docs.title: R PRO-1 Home Assistant zone configuration
How to tune the R PRO-1 using Home Assistant
docs.text:
Your R PRO-1 has two mmWave sensors that both need to be tuned

The Apollo R PRO-1 comes with an LD2450 mmWave sensor and an optional secondary LD2412 mmWave sensor.

The LD2450 tracks up to three targets in up to three zones, but can have issues with "still detection".

The optional LD2412 mmWave sensor gives you perfect still detection for one target at up to 9 meters, so it's a great addition to the sensor.

docs.title: LD2450 configuration
docs.text:
You can enter the X and Y coordinates for each LD2450 zone manually in Home Assistant, or directly on the device's web page by visiting its IP address or hostname.local. The steps below set up your zones in Home Assistant.

Prefer a phone app?

It's much easier to tune using the HLK Radartool App, and we suggest using that to set up your LD2450 instead.

Drawing zones with the Apollo mmWave dashboard?

Skip these steps and leave LD2450 Zone Type on Disabled. The dashboard's zone map replaces the radar's built-in zones. On Detection, the radar reports only people inside the zones you enter here, and with none set it reports nobody, so the map stays empty.

1. Go to Settings → Devices & services, open the ESPHome integration, and click the name of your new device.

2. Scroll down until you see LD2450 Zone Type and choose Detection from the drop-down menu.

3. Enter the X and Y coordinates for each zone.

Helpful hints for understanding LD2450 zones

  • X1 must always be less than X2, and Y1 must always be less than Y2.
  • The Y axis is simpler, since it's never negative.
  • The X axis is where you can get tripped up, especially when both values are negative: -3456 is less than -2345.
  • If you use the Plotly chart from the main R PRO-1 zone page, it still draws the rectangles even if the X1/X2 and Y1/Y2 values are reversed, so check the order yourself.
  • Zones can't overlap.

Your LD2450 now detects targets in the zones you entered.

docs.title: LD2412 configuration
docs.text: To tune the optional LD2412, follow the LD2412 Configuration steps on the main R PRO-1 Home Assistant zone page.

docs.title: R PRO-1 Home Assistant zone configuration
How to tune the R PRO-1 using Home Assistant
docs.text:
Your R PRO-1 has two unique mmWave sensors that both need to be tuned!

The R PRO-1 comes with an LD2450 mmWave sensor and an optional secondary LD2412 mmWave sensor.

The LD2450 allows for up to three targets tracked in up to three zones but can have issues with "still detection".

The optional LD2412 mmWave sensor allows you to have perfect still detection for one target at up to 9 meters so it's a great addition to the sensor.

Prefer a guided dashboard?

The Apollo mmWave integration gives your R PRO-1 a dashboard tab where you draw LD2450 zones over live targets and tune the LD2412 gates with a Calibrate with empty room button. The Apollo mmWave dashboard guide walks you through it as a guided alternative to the manual steps below. If you draw zones there, leave LD2450 Zone Type on Disabled instead of entering zones below: the dashboard's zone map replaces the radar's built-in zones, and its Radar setup card offers Set Zone Type to Disabled when it isn't.

Manually enter in the X and Y coordinates for each zone in Home Assistant or directly from the device's webserver by visiting the IP address or hostname.local. It's much easier to tune using the HLK Radartool App and we suggest using that to set up your R PRO-1 LD2450.

docs.title: LD2450 configuration
docs.text:
Follow these steps to add a Plotly card that shows your LD2450 targets, then set up your zones in Home Assistant.

1. Install HACS.

2. Download Plotly inside HACS.

3. Enter your device’s full name and optionally customize the names of the three zones using the tool below. Then click Generate YAML and Copy YAML.If you're unsure of your device name, go to Settings → Devices & services → ESPHome, select your device, and look for the full name. Unless you’ve renamed it, it will likely be something like "apollo_r_pro_1_eth_593904", with six random characters at the end.

4. Head to a dashboard view and click the pencil icon to edit dashboard then click one of the large "+" signs, type in manual, and click on it.

5. Delete any text in the custom card then paste the YAML you copied above and click save when finished. You should now have a custom card that looks like the card below!

6. Head to the ESPHome integration page (Settings → Devices & services → ESPHome).

7. Click device as shown in the image below

8. Scroll down until you get to the Configuration section and you see the empty boxes for zones 1-3 for both X and Y coordinates.

Suggested settings

  • Multi Target Tracking toggled on helps it detect up to three targets better.
  • Zone Type allows you to select Disabled, Detection, or Filter.
  • Disabled: Disable zone area detection.
  • Detection: Only detects targets in the specified zone. With no zones set, it detects nobody.
  • Filter: Excludes a zone from detection.

9. Now we can input our Zone 1-3 X and Y values to make our zones. Using the visual card from above, we can walk, sit, or stand in the area where we want to create a detection or non-detection zone. Input values for X are -4860 mm to 4860 mm, and the Y values are 0 mm to 7560 mm.

Helpful Hints to understand zones better!

  • X1 must always be less than X2, and Y1 must always be less than Y2.

  • The Y axis is easier since it's never negative.

  • The X axis is where you can get tripped up, especially when both values are negative: -3456 is less than -2345.
  • The Plotly chart will still render the rectangles even if the X1/X2 and Y1/Y2 values are reversed.
  • The zones cannot overlap.

10. If you use the imperial system (Freedom Units) then you will need to do this step. Metric users can skip this. For the targets to show up correctly we first need to update the Target 1-3 X and Y measurements from inches (in) to millimeters (mm). Find Target 1-3 X and Y under the Sensors section and select them. You will want to update all 3 X and Y target values.

11. Select the Settings cog in the top right.

12. Change the unit of measurement to mm and select Update.

13. Your X and Y Targets will now look like this.

14. Now you should see targets on the card.

15. Now we can make zones around the targets where you want to Detect presence or filter them out.

Tip for zone configuration resetting

If your zone configurations are not saved when restarting the device then try turning on the LD2450 Bluetooth for a few seconds and then turning it off again. You can also try toggling on LD2450 Multi Target Tracking. This should wake up the mmWave module and retrieve your saved zones

docs.title: LD2412 configuration
docs.text:
Follow these steps to switch the LD2412 to Engineering mode and tune its gates in Home Assistant.

1. Go to Settings → Devices & services → ESPHome and click 1 device below the Apollo R PRO-1.

2. Scroll down until you see "LD2412 Mode" and change it from "Normal" to "Engineering".

The LD2412 can be tuned using the steps below to work perfectly in your environment!

The LD2412 has "gates" at 0.75 meter increments starting at g0 and ending at g13. These gates allow you to raise the threshold needed to trigger occupancy in each 0.75 meter increment.

This is very useful in scenarios where you want to tune out a fan, a cat sitting on the stairs, etc.

3. Scroll down to the Diagnostic section and you will see "LD2412 g00 move energy" through "LD2412 g13 still energy" are showing percentages from 0-100%.

4. Scroll up to the Configuration section and identify the threshold sliders for g0-g13 for both moving and still energy.

Moving the gate still and move threshold slider to the right increases the amount of energy needed to trigger the sensor. Do this if you want the gate to be less sensitive.

Moving the gate still and move threshold slider to the left decreases the amount of energy needed to trigger the sensor. Do this if you want the gate to be more sensitive.

docs.title: R PRO-1 HLKRadarTool app zone configuration
How to tune mmWave using HLKRadarTool
LD2450 configuration
docs.text:
Ensure that the LD2450 firmware version is V2.02.23090617 or later for proper integration functionality.

The newer version of the firmware includes an "auto calibrate" function so you might want to test it out!

The HLK-LD2450 mmWave sensor is used in the R PRO-1. Click Here for the datasheet.

iPhoneAndroid

Click here to download

Click here to download

Follow these steps to turn on the LD2450's Bluetooth and set up its zones in the HLKRadarTool app.

1. Head to the ESPHome integration page (Settings → Devices & services → ESPHome) then select your R PRO-1 and scroll down until you see LD2450 Bluetooth.

Shown on an MTR-1; the R PRO-1 has the same LD2450 Bluetooth switch.

2. Open the HLKRadarTool App and select your device.

You need to be close to your device!

The LD2450 mmWave sensor is a very tiny sensor with no external antenna, which means it cannot connect to Bluetooth devices unless they are very close. Sometimes this means you need to be within a few feet of the sensor to connect directly to it!

3. Select Set in the top right.

Drawing zones with the Apollo mmWave dashboard?

In step 4, pick Close detection instead of Area Detection (LD2450 Zone Type Disabled in Home Assistant). The dashboard's zone map replaces the app's areas. On Area Detection, the radar reports only people inside the app's areas, so anyone else is missing from the map, and Area Filtering hides the people inside them.

4. Enable Area Detection (drawing zones on the Apollo mmWave dashboard instead? Pick Close detection and skip the areas; see the tip above), then toggle Area 1, 2, and 3 to display a colored box with the matching number. You can press and hold the box to move or resize it as needed. Once your zones are configured, click Submit. You should see a confirmation message: "Setup successfully."

There are three ways to use your R PRO-1!

You can use any of these three choices to control your R PRO-1 differently. The most common option is "Detection" which lets you set up three areas and track three targets within them.Disabled: Disables multi-zone area detection and tracks one big area.Detection: Only detects targets within each of the three zones.Filter: Excludes a zone from detection and detects presence everywhere else.

Disabled allows you to use the sensor as a "basic" presence sensor and "Filter" lets you filter out an area and detect everything else, which is useful to avoid a fan!

Helpful Hints to understand zones better!

  • X1 must always be less than X2, and Y1 must always be less than Y2.

  • The Y axis is easier since it's never negative.

  • The X axis is where you can get tripped up, especially when both values are negative: -3456 is less than -2345.
  • The Plotly chart will still render the rectangles even if the X1/X2 and Y1/Y2 values are reversed.
  • The zones cannot overlap.

docs.title: Dashboard card setup
docs.text:
Follow these steps to add a Plotly card that shows your R PRO-1's targets and zones on a dashboard.

1. Install HACS.

2. Download Plotly inside HACS.

3. Enter your device’s full name and optionally customize the names of the three zones using the tool below. ** ** Then click Generate YAML and Copy YAML.If you're unsure of your device name, go to Settings → Devices & services → ESPHome, select your device, and look for the full name. Unless you’ve renamed it, it will likely be something like "apollo_r_pro_1_eth_593904", with six random characters at the end.
